title: Hospital sewers may be breeding grounds for dangerous superbugs, study finds
summary: A Nature Communications study found hospital wastewater promotes antibiotic-resistant E. coli, with bacteria on sewer pipes three times as resistant.
story: Hospital wastewater has been shown to promote the growth of antibiotic-resistant bacteria, potentially making sewer systems hotspots for antimicrobial resistance, according to a new Swedish study published in Nature Communications.

Hospital wastewater has been shown to promote the growth of antibiotic-resistant bacteria, potentially making sewer systems hotspots for antimicrobial resistance, according to a new Swedish study published in Nature Communications.
Antibiotics taken by patients can pass through their bodies and enter hospital sewer systems, creating conditions that favor the growth of resistant bacteria.

Antibiotic resistance occurs when bacteria develop the ability to survive drugs designed to kill them, making some infections harder to treat. More than 9.3 million drug-resistant infections occur in the U.S. each year, resulting in more than 39,000 deaths, according to the CDC's 2026 Antimicrobial Resistance Threats Report.
DANGEROUS DRUG-RESISTANT FUNGUS SPREADS ACROSS US, REACHING 27 STATES
How hospital wastewater promotes antibiotic resistance
The researchers conducted a study involving wastewater from 10 hospitals and eight municipal wastewater treatment plants.
They wanted to determine whether hospital wastewater actually promoted the growth of antibiotic-resistant bacteria, rather than simply carrying resistant bacteria from patients.
Hospital wastewater has been shown to promote the growth of antibiotic-resistant bacteria, potentially making sewer systems hotspots for antimicrobial resistance. (iStock)

First, the researchers filtered hospital wastewater to remove existing bacteria, then exposed other bacteria to the filtered water in laboratory experiments. All 10 hospital samples significantly favored the growth of E. coli strains resistant to ciprofloxacin and cefotaxime, two antibiotics used to treat bacterial infections.
None of the eight municipal wastewater samples showed the same effect.
DEATH REPORTED IN E COLI OUTBREAK LINKED TO CALIFORNIA PUMPKIN PATCH AS MORE CASES EMERGE
This suggested that something in the wastewater itself was helping antibiotic-resistant bacteria thrive, according to the researchers.

The team also placed plastic plates in sewer pipes to study bacteria growing on their surfaces. After 30 days, bacteria growing on surfaces inside the pipes were about three times as likely to be resistant to the two antibiotics as bacteria in the surrounding wastewater. This pattern was not observed in municipal sewers.
The researchers conducted a study involving wastewater from 10 hospitals and eight municipal wastewater treatment plants. (iStock)

The researchers also measured antibiotic levels in the wastewater and tested whether those same concentrations helped resistant bacteria grow in laboratory experiments. They found that ciprofloxacin was a major contributor, while cefotaxime also played a role.
BEACHGOERS WARNED AFTER DEADLY 'FLESH-EATING' BACTERIA KILLS 5 IN SOUTHERN STATE

"The discovery [suggests] that hospital sewers could be a spawning ground for bacteria that are difficult to treat with antibiotics," Joakim Larsson, professor of environmental pharmacology at the University of Gothenburg and Director of Centre for Antibiotic Resistance Research, told Fox News Digital.
"The patients’ need for antibiotics must not be compromised."

"Knowing where resistant bacteria are promoted — and where they are less likely to be — is crucial when deciding how resources and efforts should be allocated to limit risks for antibiotic resistance development."

The study had several limitations. All sampling sites were in Sweden, and researchers focused primarily on E. coli and a limited number of antibiotics, so the findings may not apply to all bacteria or locations.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

The sewer experiment lasted approximately 30 days, leaving longer-term effects unclear. The study also did not determine whether the growth of resistant bacteria in hospital sewers leads to more infections in patients or surrounding communities.
Although the study did not directly link hospital wastewater to human infections, Larsson said resistant bacteria could potentially reach people through contaminated water.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
"When it rains heavily, treatment plants are typically overloaded, and release untreated or partially untreated wastewater with lots of bacteria," Larsson told Fox News Digital.

"If people get in contact with such waters, they can acquire those bacteria and then continue spreading them from person to person," he went on. "One thing that remains uncertain is how much you need to be exposed for resistant bacteria to colonize your gut or infect you."
Preventing antibiotic resistance
The researchers identified two possible approaches to reducing antibiotic resistance in hospital sewers.
One involves using alternative antibiotics that are less likely to pass through patients' bodies unchanged and promote the growth of resistant bacteria in wastewater.
All 10 hospital samples significantly favored the growth of E. coli strains resistant to ciprofloxacin and cefotaxime, two antibiotics used to treat bacterial infections. (iStock)

"But – and it is an important but – the patients’ need for antibiotics must not be compromised," Larsson said, emphasizing that equally effective alternatives may not always be available, and patients' medical needs must come first.

The second approach involves treating wastewater at hospitals to remove antibiotics that promote resistance, particularly fluoroquinolones and beta-lactams (two classes of antibiotics used to treat bacterial infections), while also removing harmful bacteria.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Larsson said treating wastewater at municipal plants would likely be less effective because antibiotic concentrations are high enough to favor resistant bacteria, primarily in hospital sewers.
Existing technologies can remove antibiotics from wastewater, but they can be costly and require additional treatment, he noted.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
"When we know more about the drivers, we think it might be possible to develop technical solutions that are targeted and hopefully less expensive," Larsson added.
Fox News Digital reached out to the American Hospital Association requesting comment.
Melissa Rudy is senior health editor and a member of the lifestyle team at Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to melissa.rudy@fox.com.

title: Ozempic and Zepbound users face 6 rebound risks after stopping, doctor warns
summary: Thinking of quitting a GLP-1? A physician outlines six risks, from weight regain and muscle loss to worsening biomarkers and mental health consequences.
story: Internal medicine physician Dr. Frank Dumont discusses why patients may experience renewed cravings, changes in body composition and worsening blood sugar levels when discontinuing popular injectable treatments for obesity and diabetes.
While GLP-1 medications like Ozempic, Wegovy and Zepbound have reshaped weight management and diabetes control, research shows that many patients stop taking them within a year.
Research has found that cycling off these medications can bring potential rebound risks, ranging from rapid weight regain to the loss of cardiovascular protection.

Dr. Frank Dumont, internal medicine physician and executive medical director at Virta Health in San Francisco, spoke with Fox News Digital about why patients stop taking GLP-1s, the potential risks and how to maintain progress afterward.
TYPE 2 DIABETES PATIENTS 21 TIMES MORE LIKELY TO ACHIEVE REMISSION WITH INTENSIVE LIFESTYLE CHANGES
Why patients stop
Some patients may stop taking GLP-1 medications because of medical concerns or side effects, while others prefer not to remain on long-term medication, Dumont said.
Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, constipation and diarrhea.

"Those types of things can become troublesome enough that people actually have a hard time eating enough food to get good nourishment," he told Fox News Digital. "Working with your physician to make a decision about whether it's right for you to stay on the medicine or not is important."
Other serious side effects, like acute pancreatitis, would prompt immediate discontinuation of the drug.
4 SIMPLE HABITS CAN HELP SLOW MUSCLE LOSS AS YOU AGE, FITNESS EXPERT SAYS
"We know that's fairly rare, but if the pancreas becomes involved, that is not a good thing," Dumont said. "It can be very serious. It can even be life-threatening."
Certain GLP-1 medications carry a warning about thyroid tumors based on animal studies, though the risk in humans remains unknown.
"When people take the GLP-1 medications, they lose weight, but they tend to lose both fat mass and lean muscle mass."
These medications should not be used by people with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or a condition called multiple endocrine neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2).
Dumont outlined six potential risks patients may face after stopping a GLP-1.
No. 1: Return of hunger and cravings
The most immediate side effect patients notice after stopping a GLP-1 is the return of intense cravings and a sharp spike in appetite, often referred to as "food noise," according to Dumont.
Many patients assume they can treat GLP-1s like a short-term prescription, taking the drug to hit a target weight or blood sugar goal and then stopping, the doctor noted.
Hunger and cravings typically increase after stopping a GLP-1, the doctor said. (iStock)

However, major medical organizations, including the American Medical Association (AMA) and the Obesity Medicine Association, classify obesity as a chronic condition that typically requires ongoing management.

"Unless you have significantly changed what you're doing in terms of the types of foods you're eating, it's likely you'll go back to the same foods you were eating before, and hunger and cravings will go up," Dumont said.
No. 2: Weight regain
It is typical for GLP-1 users to experience weight regain after quitting, according to Dumont.
In the STEP 1 trial extension, participants regained about two-thirds of the weight they had lost within a year of stopping semaglutide and lifestyle interventions.
WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS MAY FIGHT 7 SERIOUS HEALTH PROBLEMS BEFORE THE POUNDS EVEN COME OFF

In the SURMOUNT-4 trial for tirzepatide, patients who were switched to a placebo after 36 weeks of treatment regained more than half the weight they had lost over the following year, even while receiving diet and exercise counseling.
"That's just so devastating for people who felt like they'd finally found a solution that would work," Dumont said.
No. 3: Change in biomarkers

Biomarkers — which are measurable indicators of what’s happening inside the body, such as blood sugar, blood pressure and cholesterol levels — tend to improve while taking a GLP-1, which is beneficial for those with prediabetes or diabetes.
When a GLP-1 is stopped, these markers can reverse if not countered with a change in diet, according to Dumont.
Early trials have found that people regained more than two-thirds of the weight they lost while taking a GLP-1 within a year of stopping the medication. (iStock)
Improvements in fatty liver disease may also fade after treatment stops, the doctor said.

"We know that these medications can help to decrease some of that steatotic or fatty liver disease that occurs," he noted. "And when you go off the medicine, if you go back to eating the way you did before, those numbers have a tendency to worsen."
No. 4: Worsening body composition
Weight loss while taking GLP-1 medications can include a loss of muscle, raising concerns about body composition and long-term physical function, according to Dumont.
"When people take the GLP-1 medications, they lose weight, but they tend to lose both fat mass and lean muscle mass," he told Fox News Digital.
In a body-composition study of tirzepatide, about 25% of the weight lost was lean mass, which includes muscle and other nonfat tissue. The remaining 75% was fat.
Dumont expressed concern that patients who regain weight after stopping treatment may not fully replace the muscle they lost.
Studies have linked GLP-1s to a reduced risk of chronic health conditions like cardiovascular disease and stroke. (iStock)

"So, there's a bit of a ratcheting-down effect if someone is on and off these medications, where they lose fat and muscle, stop the medicine, regain fat, go back on the medicine, and lose fat and muscle," he added.
The doctor emphasized that preserving muscle is important for metabolism, injury prevention and everyday activities.
No. 5: Mental health effects
In addition to the physical consequences, Dumont noted that stopping a weight-loss drug can take a heavy toll on mental health.
Many patients have spent years cycling through diets and programs without lasting success, often viewing GLP-1s as a final solution, according to the doctor.
In addition to the physical consequences, the doctor noted that stopping a weight-loss drug can take a heavy toll on mental health. (iStock)

When the medication isn't right for them — adding to a history of past weight-loss setbacks — experiencing a "regression on all fronts" can be "really devastating from a mental health standpoint," Dumont said.
"It can make you feel disheartened and like you don’t have the control you thought you did," he added.
No. 6: Loss of health protection

An observational study published in BMJ Medicine found that adults with type 2 diabetes who stopped GLP-1 treatment had a higher risk of major cardiovascular events than those who continued. Longer periods without treatment were associated with greater risk.
Dumont noted that the stakes of stopping a GLP-1 go far beyond weight, pointing to the broader risk of losing metabolic benefits.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
While taking a GLP-1, lower inflammation and improved cholesterol and blood sugar levels help reduce the risk of major events like heart attacks and strokes, the doctor said.

"But again, if you stop the medicine and you haven't changed the way that you eat, then all of those numbers can worsen … and that can then increase the risk of those bad things happening — things that can be devastating from a life quality standpoint, but also can shorten your life," he warned.
For those with a genetic pre-disposition to an endocrine-type cancer, Williams suggested that a GLP-1 might not be a "good option." (iStock)

In a separate interview with Fox News Digital, Dr. Jason Williams, an interventional radiologist-oncologist at the Williams Cancer Institute, confirmed that some GLP-1s can increase cancer risk, particularly in endocrine cancers – but these medications can also reduce inflammation and other markers that could reduce the risk of cancer.
"So, it's kind of a balance," he said. "Most [cancers] are more fed by this inflammatory pattern that may be associated with fat and other cytokines that the GLPs can help reduce."
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
Williams, author of "The Longevity Primer," projected that the future of GLP-1s will include more flexible, individualized, "on and off" use, instead of dosing daily.
"We've been too conditioned to think that you take a medicine every day, but it's not really how things work for people," he said. "I think we have to look at things like phases and waves."

"The GLP-1 is not the only solution," the doctor said. "It needs to be coupled with ... a way of eating that's going to work for you for the long term that allows you to stop the medicine successfully if you need to." (iStock)
Making your progress last
Reaching metabolic goals and making lasting lifestyle changes may help patients maintain their progress after stopping a GLP-1, according to Dumont.
"We actually have peer-reviewed published data demonstrating that you can indeed stop one of these medications when you reach your metabolic goals," he said.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The Virta-affiliated observational study examined selected patients with type 2 diabetes in a structured nutrition program, so the findings may not apply to all GLP-1 users.
The doctor recommended adopting sustainable eating habits before stopping a GLP-1.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"The GLP-1 is not the only solution," he said. "It needs to be coupled with ... a way of eating that's going to work for you for the long term that allows you to stop the medicine successfully if you need to."
Dumont recommended working with the prescribing clinician on a plan for stopping treatment and monitoring weight and blood sugar afterward.
Angelica Stabile is a lifestyle reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Recent service outages not state-sponsored attacks, DNI Jay Clayton testifies
summary: DNI Jay Clayton told the House Homeland Security Committee recent U.S. service outages stem from maintenance, not a coordinated state-sponsored attack.
story: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton outlines national security threats including terrorism and Iranian plotting, saying recent cyber service disruptions are not state-sponsored attacks, nor are they related.

Recent service outages across U.S. systems stem from routine technical and maintenance issues – not a coordinated foreign cyberattack, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton testified Wednesday, even as he warned lawmakers that "superintelligence" is rapidly escalating the speed and sophistication of future cyber threats.

"Based on what we know today, after a great deal of digital diligence, these are separate service outages associated with maintenance and technical changes, " Clayton told the House Homeland Security Committee's "Worldwide Threats to the Homeland: 25 Years After 9/11" hearing. "They are not a coordinated or state-sponsored attack."

Clayton acknowledged public concern over the timing of the recent outages, telling the panel that the American people are right to ask questions, but intelligence reviews point away from foreign interference.
THE OUTAGES AMERICA HAS SUFFERED WEREN'T AN ATTACK, BUT THE NEXT FAILURE COULD BE

Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and Deputy FBI Director Christopher Raia testify during a House Homeland Security Committee hearing on "Worldwide Threats to the Homeland: 25 Years after 9/11" on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C., on Nov. 18, 2026. (Brendan Smialowski / AFP via Getty Images)

"We have no indication that these events are related," Clayton said in response to persistent questioning from Rep. Dan Goldman, D-N.Y. "But let me answer something that the American people should know, which is the speed of compute and the level of capability of applications that use that compute is increasing substantially, which means legacy systems that were old six months ago or a year are a lot older."
The intelligence community remains on alert and continues to monitor for any malicious cyber activity targeting U.S. networks or law enforcement partners, Clayton said in his opening statement.

"After doing a great deal of due diligence inside the government with the private sector, with people in the private sector whose job is cybersecurity, we have no indication that these incidents are related, that they're coordinated," Clayton reiterated in the question and answer session of the hearing. "We also have no indication that they're a result of a state-sponsored malign actor."
TIMELINE: AMERICA HITS A TECH WALL AS OUTAGES CRIPPLE EMAIL, GROUND FLIGHTS AND DISRUPT MAJOR BANKS

Beyond the immediate outages, the intelligence chief warned lawmakers that rapid advancements in artificial intelligence – also referred to as "superintelligence" – are fundamentally altering the digital battlefield and raising the stakes for homeland defense.

"Let me note that superintelligence is reshaping the cybersecurity landscape, " Clayton said. "It is sharply increasing speed, scale, and sophistication of offensive and defensive cyber operations. And it's not just cyber. This goes to national security. It goes to the battlefield and it goes to commerce. Superintelligence is changing the way we do business, the way we fight wars and the way we combat terrorism every day."
GOVERNMENT INVESTIGATORS FIND AI PLATFORMS PRODUCE TERROR PLOT PLANS IN UNDERCOVER OP

During his opening remarks, Clayton outlined a broader heightened threat environment 25 years after the Sept. 11 attacks. While declining to discuss classified intelligence in an open setting, he noted that full briefings have been provided to the Gang of Eight and congressional intelligence committees.

title: Florida eyes poaching NYPD officers after Mamdani dismantles elite unit
summary: Sen. Ashley Moody invites NYPD Strategic Response Group officers to Florida after Zohran Mamdani announced the counterterrorism unit's disbandment.
story: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani was pressed on why he is not retraining NYPD officers on de-escalation instead of sending an unarmed civilian unit to handle protests.

Florida’s former top law enforcement officer issued a call for members of an NYPD counterterrorism unit to relocate to the Sunshine State as many New Yorkers already have, after New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Councilman Chi Ossé announced the disbandment of the specialized unit.

Mamdani and Ossé, D-Brooklyn, announced this week that the Strategic Response Group (SRG) will be dissolved in alignment with a key campaign promise by the mayor, as critics, including former NYPD Commissioner Bill Bratton, who created the unit, warn it will make the nation’s largest city more dangerous.
"Florida is always looking for well-qualified new officers," Sen. Ashley Moody, R-Fla., said in reaction to the news.
MAMDANI PREPARES TO FULFILL PROMISE TO AXE NYPD UNIT RESPONSIBLE FOR CONTROLLING PROTEST VIOLENCE
"The Sunshine State welcomes members of the NYPD Strategic Response Group to join our mission of protecting Florida communities," said Moody, who was previously the state’s attorney general.
NYPD officers who accept the invitation would add to the nearly 376,000 New Yorkers who relocated to Florida between 2019 and 2023, according to figures reported by New York's WPIX-11 News.
Miami-Dade County Commissioner Roberto Gonzalez, a Republican, also issued a call for disillusioned NYPD officers to relocate.
"In Florida, it’s always our priority to back the brave men and women that wear the badge. Miami-Dade [Sheriff’s Office] is the best in the country. NYPD’s finest: We’re hiring," he said.
Fox News Digital reached out to Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis, a Republican, and Florida Gov.-elect Byron Donalds, R-Fla., for further comment but did not receive an immediate response.

The invitations come months after another Florida law enforcement leader rented Times Square advertising space to draw NYPD officers southward after Mamdani defeated former Gov. Andrew Cuomo, D-N. Y., and activist Curtis Sliwa in the 2025 mayoral election.
Volusia County Sheriff Michael Chitwood — who hails from Philadelphia — publicly encouraged NYPD officers to come to Daytona Beach.
"Dear NYPD, Sunny Florida is waiting," read one of the billboards from the Volusia County Sheriff’s Foundation. The displays in Times Square included a QR code for officers to apply on the spot.
"Serve a community that appreciates you," it went on.
"You’re going to get support here, and you’re going to have a tremendous quality of life," Chitwood told Fox’s Orlando affiliate.
MAMDANI UNVEILS SWEEPING NYPD USE-OF-FORCE REVIEW, BUT STOPS SHORT OF FULFILLING KEY CAMPAIGN PROMISES
Chi Ossé, a New York City Council member, speaks at a campaign rally for mayoral candidate Zohran Mamdani at United Palace in New York City on Oct. 13, 2025. (Christian Monterrosa/Bloomberg)

On Monday, Mamdani said in a video announcing the end of the SRG that counterterrorism and protest response should have separate enforcement entities, while Ossé added that the government has a responsibility to protect constitutional rights and "keep communities safe."
"Those priorities are not in conflict," Ossé said, as the two announced a replacement agency within the mayor’s office called the Community Dialogue and De-escalation Division (CDDD).
MAMDANI CLASHES WITH DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS' PUSH TO ABOLISH POLICE AND PRISONS
The CDDD will be staffed with unarmed civilians without arrest powers who will seek to engage in dialogue with protesters while reserving the right to call in uniformed police if necessary.
The two referenced their own prior arrests, remarking deadpan, "We both know something about that," when laying out how officers can still respond to arrest people involved in "civil disobedience."

Ossé was arrested in April while protesting the scheduled eviction of a constituent, while then-Assemblyman Mamdani was arrested in 2023 during a traffic-blocking protest outside the Brooklyn home of Sen. Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y.
Fox News Digital reached out to the NYPD and Mamdani’s office for comment.

Mamdani's office responded by sharing a transcript of his news conference on the SRG. At one point, Mamdani said, "The point here is looking for de-escalation, looking for engagement and dialogue, and that being a constant both in advance and during. And when you're asking about — as the march continues, if you have a sense that this march is transforming into something else, then it's not for civilians to be on the front lines of that."
Some fellow Democrats also criticized Mamdani for the decision.

New York City Councilman James Gennaro, D-Queens, said on X that transferring the SRG’s responsibilities to the new division the mayor described raised concerns about whether the NYPD will be able to "maintain the specialized training and experience to respond to volatile and potentially violent situations."
"It also raises concerns about the city’s ability to respond to large-scale events and major incidents, including active-shooter attacks," Gennaro said.
SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani listens to reporters' questions during a press conference at Athens Square Park on Nov. 17, 2026, in New York City. The appearance came a day after Mamdani and NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch announced plans to disband the department's Strategic Response Group. (Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)

Former NYPD Commissioner Bill Bratton, who served under Mayors Rudy Giuliani and Bill de Blasio, said the city can reorganize the NYPD but not "reorganize away the threats that require" the SRG’s specialized response.

"As the commissioner who created the 600-officer Strategic Response Group and the 500-officer Counterterrorism Critical Response Command, I know why we built them — and what they were meant to do," Bratton said on X after publishing an op-ed on the matter in the New York Post.
Born and raised in Allentown, Pennsylvania, worked in both the New York and Washington bureaus for Fox News since 2013.

title: Americans misled on Social Security for decades as clock counts down on benefits, explosive report reveals
summary: Sen. Ron Johnson says Americans are being scammed by Social Security, calling the program a legal Ponzi scheme that is hurtling toward insolvency by 2032.
story: Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., Senate Budget Committee chair, claims that Social Security is nothing more than a "Legal Ponzi Scheme." (CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)

FIRST ON FOX: A Senate Republican is sounding the alarm that Americans are being "scammed" by the government’s handling of Social Security, and warned that it’s too late to change the trajectory of the decades-old safety net.

Senate Budget Committee Chair Ron Johnson, R-Wis., claimed in a new report called "Social Security: The Reality… a Legal Ponzi Scheme," that the federal government has been duping Americans on what really happens with taxpayer money that flows into the program.

As Social Security hurtles toward insolvency — meaning the fund will run out of money and be unable to pay 100% of scheduled benefits on time — Johnson warned in the report first obtained by Fox News Digital that "once a Ponzi scheme begins to collapse, it can’t be fixed."
AMERICA’S RETIREMENT SYSTEM IS BROKEN. TRUMP MAY HAVE FOUND A BOLD FIX

"It can only be liquidated, with late investors often receiving only pennies on the dollar for their end-of-scheme investments," Johnson said. "Their only hope is that an underlying financial entity can provide a backstop to limit their losses."

Johnson’s report projected that by 2032, when Social Security is expected to become insolvent, there will be a roughly $511 billion Social Security shortfall, equal to roughly 21% of the projected $2.4 trillion total federal deficit that year.

The main thrust of Johnson’s report, which he wrote himself, is that Americans have been convinced that Social Security and the portion that comes from their paychecks that fund it, known as the Federal Insurance Contributions Act — the percentage deducted from a person’s paycheck that helps fund Social Security and Medicare — is a retirement account that grows over time.
CONGRESS SPENDS $7 TRILLION. HERE’S HOW THAT MATH WORKS OUT IF YOU THINK OF JUST $100

Johnson, chairman of the Senate Budget Committee for another two months, countered that Americans’ tax dollars aren’t in a "lock box" designed to flourish, but instead that 6.2% from every person’s paycheck goes to pay for other peoples’ benefits.
"People often say, ‘Don’t touch Social Security, that’s my money,’" Johnson wrote. "Actually, it’s not."
"Your money was spent to pay current beneficiaries or fund other government programs as soon as it was collected from your paycheck."

"Your future benefits will be paid with the money collected from your sons and daughters working at that time, plus money borrowed from the public now that Social Security is running deficits," he continued.
Johnson blamed decisions from Congress in the past, like not investing surpluses in the program into stocks or promising increasingly expensive benefits with few workers in the workforce.
GOP FISCAL HAWK SOUNDS ALARM ON 'OUT OF CONTROL' FEDERAL SPENDING, SAYING 'BOTH PARTIES HAVE FAILED US'

Johnson acknowledged that "Social Security cannot be fundamentally fixed as a retirement investment fund because it never was one," and noted that under current law, once the program’s trust fund is depleted, which is estimated to hit in 2032, benefits will be reduced.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The solution: "repeal that portion of the law that reduces Social Security benefits and quit scaring seniors."
"We should then roll up our sleeves and begin seriously addressing the main problem — our massive debt and deficits," Johnson wrote.
Alex Miller is a writer for Fox News Digital covering the U.S. Senate.

title: Jeffries survives Dem vote to secure speaker position as progressive resistance clouds his chances
summary: House Democrats nominated Hakeem Jeffries for speaker despite progressive backlash, setting up a January vote that could test party unity.
story: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries tells Fox News that he is going to speak to every member ahead of leadership elections to rally support to be selected as Speaker of the House.

House Democrats selected Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., as their nominee for speaker of the House in the 120th Congress following the party's sweeping midterm victories, a senior House Democratic staffer confirmed to Fox News Digital.

Despite growing opposition from progressives over his leadership and ties to the Democratic establishment, Jeffries survived the secret-ballot vote on Wednesday in a "landslide," according to the staffer, advancing him as the party's nominee to lead the majority in the new Congress. Only 11 Democrats voted against his speaker nomination.
The New York lawmaker must now win a full House vote in January to secure the position.
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., speaks during a press conference on Capitol Hill on Nov. 3, 2025, in Washington, D.C. (Roberto Schmidt/Getty Images)
SENATE DEM CHALLENGING SEN CHUCK SCHUMER FOR LEADERSHIP POST BACKS HAKEEM JEFFRIES FOR HOUSE SPEAKER

Jeffries ran unopposed for the nomination, although recent reports indicated Democratic congressional offices had been inundated with calls from frustrated voters urging lawmakers to select an alternative candidate.

After he cleared the vote, the committee room where the incoming class of Democratic members, made up of re-elected and newly elected caucus members, erupted in cheering and clapping immediately following the vote.
"It was a blowout number," Rep. Bennie Thompson, D-Miss., told Fox News Digital after the vote.

The Democratic leader has faced criticism from progressive members of his party over his support for Israel and his ties to corporate political action committees, which critics argue reflect the priorities of the Democratic establishment rather than the party's progressive base.

Rep.-elect Don Leonard, D-Ohio, who flipped a district carried by Trump in 2024, told local media that he would be "shopping for a new leader" if Jeffries did not commit to changing his position on Israel.

When asked by Fox News Digital if he voted against Jeffries on Wednesday, Rep.-elect Adam Hamawy, D-N.J., a new member of the progressive caucus, declined to comment. After the vote count was reported, it was confirmed that Hamawy voted against Jeffries’ nomination.

Rep. elects Darializa Avila Chevalier, D-NY., Frederick Haynes, D-Texas, Melat Kiros, D-Colo., Donavan McKinney, D-Mich., Chris Rabb, PA, and Claire Valdez, D-N.Y., joined Hamawy in opposing Jeffries.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., speaks with reporters as he walks to his office after a press conference at the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C., on March 27, 2026. (Samuel Corum/Getty Images)
FOLLOW THE LEADER: DEMOCRATS FACE PARTY BATTLE AS DIVISIONS DEEPEN

Rep. Jonathan Jackson, D-Ill., told Fox News Digital that the members who voted against them were "unfair" as they had never seen his abilities as a legislator, minority leader and let alone Speaker of the House.
Jackson added that these new representatives probably voted against Jeffries because they were following what their constituents wanted them to do.

Rep. Josh Gottheimer, D-N.J., told Fox News Digital that these new representatives are members of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), not the Democratic Party, and have their own independent legislative agenda outside that of the establishment.

After the vote, the coalition who voted against Jeffries released a statement claiming that they opposed Jeffries' nomination because the minority leader does not represent the agenda they believe in, which includes abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and Medicare-for-all.

Democrats are preparing to use their new majority in January to immediately launch investigations, challenge President Donald Trump's policies through legislative oversight and hold congressional hearings. If Jeffries advances to speaker, he will lead that effort.
Despite the opposition, Jeffries has maintained support from prominent Democratic leaders, including former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., who publicly backed his bid for the speakership.
Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., and Rep. Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., talk on the House floor on Jan. 6, 2023. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc. via Getty Images)

Jeffries' nomination does not guarantee that he will become speaker when the new Congress convenes in January. The New York Democrat must still secure enough votes from the full House to win the position, but with the overwhelming victory on Wednesday, the path to speakership appears clearcut.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The looming vote could test whether progressive dissatisfaction with Jeffries' leadership translates into opposition on Capitol Hill or remains largely confined to grassroots activists.

The controversy also raises questions about whether incoming Democrats who campaigned against the party's establishment will ultimately support its chosen leader or demand policy concessions in exchange for their votes.
During the secret ballot session on Wednesday morning, Democrats selected Rep. Ted Lieu, D-Calif., to become the party's next caucus chair.

title: Government investigators find AI platforms produce terror plot plans in undercover op
summary: GAO investigators bypassed AI safeguards on ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok, obtaining feasible plans for terrorist attacks in under 12 hours of testing.
story: An iPhone screen photographed at close range displays four AI assistant application icons — Claude by Anthropic, ChatGPT by OpenAI, Gemini by Google and Grok by xAI — arranged in a two-by-two grid in San Ferdinando di Puglia, Italy, on May 17, 2026. (Photo Illustration by Matteo Della Torre/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Federal investigators successfully bypassed safety safeguards on four major artificial intelligence platforms, obtaining detailed plans for potentially deadly terrorist attacks in less than 12 hours, according to a government watchdog report released Wednesday.

The Government Accountability Office (GAO) found that ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok each generated information that could help carry out attacks targeting crowded locations or the nation's electrical grid during undercover testing conducted in spring 2026.

Two platforms produced plans involving improvised explosive devices intended to cause mass casualties, while the other two outlined attacks on electrical infrastructure designed to inflict economic damage.

The AI-generated responses included potential targets, locations, timing and attack methods. Although all four platforms initially activated safeguards to block or remove harmful content, investigators ultimately circumvented those protections.
CHINESE AI MODEL INVESTIGATED AFTER RESEARCHER SAYS IT PROVIDED INSTRUCTIONS FOR BIOWEAPONS, ASSASSINATIONS
A finger taps the Grok app icon on a smartphone screen in this illustration photo taken on September 17, 2026. (Photo Illustration by Matteo Della Torre/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

GAO investigators also consulted experts and conducted real-world checks to assess the plans, finding that the information provided by all four platforms was sufficiently feasible to assist someone planning an attack.
"The potential benefits of this technology are immense, but they can also benefit malicious actors," the GAO warned, citing growing risks to national and economic security.
The companies behind the platforms — OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and SpaceXAI — said they were continuing to improve their safety measures, while some raised concerns about the testing.
BIOWEAPON THREAT EXPOSED AS ANTHROPIC SOUNDS ALARM ON FOREIGN ACTORS PLOTTING VIRUS EXPERIMENTS

Anthropic acknowledged that determined users could bypass AI safeguards and said it took the findings seriously, but questioned aspects of the GAO's methodology and said it could not independently verify the results.

Google noted that investigators tested earlier versions of its models, saying, "We continue to improve our models." OpenAI welcomed the opportunity to respond to the findings and acknowledged "the work that remains," while SpaceXAI said it "continues to work diligently" to strengthen safety with each model release.
Sen. Maggie Hassan, D-N.H., at the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C., on Monday, Nov. 10, 2025. (Aaron Schwartz/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
The report, requested by Sen. Maggie Hassan, D-N.H., comes amid growing scrutiny of AI's potential misuse and renewed calls for stronger safeguards against national security threats.

"The AI public safety threat is no longer theoretical," Hassan said in a statement Wednesday. "If Congress does not act, it is a question of when – not if – a bad actor will use AI to plan and carry out a major attack."

title: Far-left groups cheer Mamdani for disbanding elite NYPD protest team

story: ‘The Five’ co-hosts comment on New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s move to disband the NYPD’s Strategic Response Group. Panelists criticize Mamdani’s decision to replace the tactical police unit with civilian-led conflict resolution teams.

Far-left radical groups, including some within tech tycoon Neville Roy Singham’s pro-CCP network, are cheering New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s decision to dissolve an elite NYPD unit responsible for handling protests.

After Mamdani announced Monday morning that he would disband the elite police department's Strategic Response Group, applause came in rapid succession from nonprofit organizations that regularly mobilize protests of ICE, Israel, capitalism and America in general.
"The mass movement has won the disbanding of NYPD’s Strategic Response Group — but the fight continues," the Party for Socialism and Liberation posted to X following the announcement.
MAMDANI PREPARES TO FULFILL PROMISE TO AXE NYPD UNIT RESPONSIBLE FOR CONTROLLING PROTEST VIOLENCE

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani listens to reporters' questions during a press conference at Athens Square Park on Nov. 17, 2026, in New York City. The appearance came a day after Mamdani and NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch announced plans to disband the department's Strategic Response Group. (Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)

"For everyone who has been kettled, beaten, pepper-sprayed or dragged onto a bus by the SRG, this is a real victory. But it was not handed down from City Hall. It was won by a mass movement that refused to let a campaign promise die quietly. The work of turning this victory into lasting change for working people is just beginning," the post added.

The Party for Socialism and Liberation is part of a protest network of activist groups tied to Singham, a Shanghai-based tech tycoon married to far-left CodePink co-founder Jodie Evans. A Fox News Digital analysis found that Singham funneled $278 million into six nonprofits, including $22.4 million to the People's Forum, the Manhattan organizing hub that works closely with the Party for Socialism and Liberation on protests.
SHANGHAI-BASED TYCOON NEVILLE ROY SINGHAM'S 'SQUAD,' BERNIE SANDERS DONATIONS RESURFACE

Fox News Digital has witnessed protest foot soldiers and field marshals from the Party for Socialism and Liberation enter and leave the People's Forum headquarters on W. 37th Street, their signs, wagons and loudspeakers in tow.

David Chung, organizing director at The People’s Forum, left, prepares for an anti-war demonstration in Union Square in New York City. Tech tycoon Neville Roy Singham, right, attends The Red Party in New York City on Feb. 14, 2018. (Rashid Umar Abbasi for Fox News Digital; Mark Sagliocco/Getty Images)

The Party for Socialism and Liberation also shares leadership with Singham-funded groups. Claudia De la Cruz, a 2024 presidential candidate for the Party for Socialism and Liberation leader, was on the People's Forum's founding board alongside Evans.

Longtime organizer Brian Becker, a self-described communist, helped build the People's Forum into a base for the Party for Socialism and Liberation and the ANSWER Coalition, and his son, Ben Becker, is editor-in-chief of the Singham-funded BreakThrough News, which also shares a home at the People’s Forum headquarters on W. 37th Street.
SINGHAM-BACKED, PRO-CHINA GROUP DROPS HUGE SUM ON MANHATTAN HQ AS FEDS PROBE SHADOWY NETWORK
By early morning, self-declared Marxist influencer and Twitch streamer Hasan Piker weighed in, saying he was "glad" the unit had been disbanded.

At 11:16 a.m., Piker posted a response to Mamdani’s message, skipping capitalizations as he wrote: "one of the hardest problems for NYC mayor is police reform. The SRG is a ‘counter terrorism’ unit that has primarily been deployed on protestors. glad the mayor is moving on this promise to disband."
HASAN PIKER NAMES PRO-CCP TYCOON SINGHAM AS FINANCIER OF 'POLITICAL MOVEMENTS' DESPITE NONPROFIT VENEER

By the afternoon, at 2:55 p.m., Nerdeen Kiswani, an anti-Israel activist who founded the organization Within Our Lifetime, responded to the announcement by calling for consequences for NYPD officers who subdued protests, while saying the disbanding is "overdue and welcome news" in a post on X.

Within Our Lifetime co-founder Nerdeen Kiswani speaks during a "Nakba 78" anti-Israel protest in Washington Square Park on May 15, 2026, in New York City, as demonstrators carrying Palestinian flags and Hamas flags gather behind her. (Asra Q. Nomani/Fox News Digital)

"The settlement gave us a way to challenge the NYPD when it violated protesters’ rights, and officers violated it anyway," Kiswani wrote. "The limits Mamdani announced today give us more specific rules to point to when we challenge police conduct. We’ll see whether the NYPD actually follows them when we’re back in the streets, especially when we’re protesting something the people in power would rather we stay quiet about."

Mamdani previously joined Kiswani in an anti-Israel protest, where calls to "globalize the intifada" rang out from the protesters in the crowd. Within Our Lifetime is not a registered nonprofit, so its tax filings and funding aren’t available to the public. Fox News Digital hasn’t identified any direct ties to the Singham network aside from joining member groups in demonstrations.

Mamdani’s announcement fulfilled a campaign promise he made to disband the group. While the Party for Socialism and Liberation says "the mass movement has won," it’s unclear whether the organization had any impact on the mayor’s decision.
MAMDANI GUTS ELITE NYPD TACTICAL UNIT, BACKS 'CIVILIAN-LED APPROACH' TO RESPONDING TO PROTESTS
Hasan Piker speaks at a press conference during day two of Web Summit Vancouver 2026 at Vancouver Convention Centre in Vancouver, Canada. (Sam Barnes/Web Summit via Sportsfile via Getty Images)

"New Yorkers exercising their constitutional right to protest should not be met with the same police response as a terrorism threat," Mamdani told reporters in a news conference announcing the changes. "We are establishing a new, civilian-led approach that prioritizes dialogue, engagement and de-escalation."
Former NYPD officers weighed in on Mamdani’s decision, saying the move would empower criminals and promote anarchy.
POLICE GROUPS CONDEMN MAMDANI OVER AXING ELITE NYPD UNIT

"I think it’s one more step towards emboldening the criminals, emboldening the anarchists and emboldening the terrorists," said James Gagliano, a retired FBI supervisory special agent and Fox News contributor who spent years working alongside the NYPD.
Protesters and counter-protesters gathered inside Washington Square Park in New York, New York, on Friday afternoon. (Rashid Umar Abbasi for Fox News Digital)

title: US launches unarmed ICBM with Trump in Asia in routine test
summary: The Air Force says it carried out a "routine" test launch of an intercontinental ballistic missile, shortly before President Trump arrived in China.
story: President Donald Trump arrives in Shenzhen, China, for historic talks with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. Former CIA station chief Dan Hoffman joins 'Fox & Friends First' to analyze the trilateral talks. He also weighs in after the U.S. launches defensive strikes against Iran.
The U.S. military carried out a test launch of an unarmed Minuteman III intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) as President Donald Trump was traveling aboard Air Force One to China.

The Air Force Global Strike Command said the "routine test" late Tuesday at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California, outside of Los Angeles, "was scheduled years ago and is not in response to world events."

"The ability to conduct these rigorous, realistic tests relies on the dedication of our Airmen and is foundational to ensuring the safety and surety of the Minuteman system," U.S. Air Force Gen. S.L. Davis, commander of Air Force Global Strike Command, said in a statement.

"Test opportunities, including this most recent launch, assess the entirety of the ICBM enterprise and provide various government agencies data to inform ICBM sustainment, engineering, and lifecycle analysis efforts," Air Force Global Strike Command added. "AFGSC has completed over 300 Minuteman III test launches to date."
US RAMPS NUCLEAR WEAPONS PRODUCTION TO COLD WAR LEVELS AS CHINA PURSUES ‘UNPRECEDENTED’ BUILDUP
An unarmed Minuteman III intercontinental ballistic missile test launch is carried out on May 20, 2026, at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California. (2nd Lt. Andrew Taller/Space Launch Delta 30)
Following the test launch, Chinese President Xi Jinping greeted Trump as he arrived in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday.
The Air Force describes the LGM-30G Minuteman III missile as the "land-based component of the U.S. nuclear triad, providing a responsive and survivable strategic deterrent.

"The current force consists of 400 Minuteman III missiles dispersed at F.E. Warren Air Force Base, Wyoming; Malmstrom Air Force Base, Montana; and Minot Air Force Base, North Dakota," the Air Force said.
NORTH KOREA MISSILE COULD PUT GUAM IN RANGE AS KIM REBUFFS TRUMP OUTREACH: EXPERT

President Donald Trump salutes next to Chinese President Xi Jinping as he arrives at Shenzhen Airport to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Leaders Summit in Shenzhen, China, on Nov. 18, 2026. (Reuters)

"Missile combat crews, consisting of two officers, are on alert around the clock in underground Launch Control Centers. A robust and redundant communications network ensures the president and U.S. Strategic Command have reliable, direct contact with each crew," the Air Force also said, noting that the Minuteman III system was first deployed in 1970 and has "evolved to meet new security challenges through more than 60 years of continuous service."
The last unarmed Minuteman III test launch happened on May 20 at Vandenberg Space Force Base.
An unarmed Minuteman III intercontinental ballistic missile launches during a previous operational test at Vandenberg Air Force Base in California. (Defense Media Activity/Web.mil)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"This launch allows us to authenticate the complete performance profile of the Minuteman III," Lt. Col. Karrie Wray, commander of the 576th Flight Test Squadron, said at the time. "It confirms the precision of the system, ensuring the reentry vehicle can be delivered to its target with pinpoint accuracy."
Fox News' Lucas Tomlinson contributed to this report.
Greg Norman is a reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: Trump’s grip on GOP faces major post-election test as his hand-picked leader faces challenge from within
summary: President Donald Trump is working to save RNC Chair Joe Gruters from a re-election challenge by co-Chair KC Crosbie after GOP midterm election losses.
story: Former Vice President Mike Pence, in an exclusive Fox News Digital interview, says GOP midterm defeat was a 'reckoning' over Trump's shift away from conservative principles

President Donald Trump's handpicked leader of the Republican National Committee (RNC) is facing a challenge from within his own leadership team after Republicans suffered sweeping losses in the midterm elections that saw even historically deep red seats flip blue in states like Texas, Mississippi and South Carolina.

RNC Chair Joe Gruters, who is seeking a full two-year term running the national party committee, will face-off with co-Chair KC Crosbie of Kentucky after Democrats captured sizable majorities in both the House and Senate and prepare to retake control in January.

Crosbie, a staunch Trump supporter, launched her bid just days after the elections, seeking to capitalize on frustration among Republicans over the party's losses and build support for a change in leadership.

"I hope to speak with each of you before then. I want to hear what you saw in your states, what you think we need to change, and how we can put our Party in a stronger position for the next election," Crosbie wrote in a letter to the 168 RNC committee members, who will vote for the next chair when the party holds its winter meeting in Arizona in mid-January.
FIRST ON FOX: PENCE LEAVES DOOR OPEN TO 2028 WHITE HOUSE RUN
Republican National Committee Chair Joe Gruters is interviewed by Fox News Digital on Sept. 8, 2026 in Dallas, Texas, on the eve of the GOP midterm convention. (Paul Steinhauser/Fox News)

Some party insiders tell Fox News that Gruters is expected to win re-election, thanks to support from President Trump — but others familiar with the mood of the RNC membership said support for Crosbie is growing.

Trump, who installed Gruters as party chair 15 months ago after he urged then-Chair Michael Whatley to run for the Senate in North Carolina, quickly endorsed him in the days after the midterms to earn a full term at the helm.

"Joe Gruters should return as Chairman of the RNC to continue to build our Party, and be a trusted partner as we MAKE AMERICA GREAT AGAIN, and ensure Free and Fair Elections," Trump wrote on social media.

A source confirmed to Fox News Digital that the president has been working behind the scenes to shore up support for Gruters and also confirmed an Axios report that the president threatened retribution against the RNC if the chair isn't re-elected.
WILL TRUMP AVOID MAKING AN ENDORSEMENT IN THE 2028 GOP NOMINATION RACE?

An aide in Gruters' political orbit told Fox News Digital that the chairman is hitting the phones and reaching out to committee members — and the calls are going well. They highlighted how the RNC had historic fundraising over the past year under Gruters' leadership and that he made over 40 campaign stops in 14 states during the midterm election's final stretch while working directly with members and state party chairs on a daily basis.
Photo of President Donald Trump, left, and Republican National Committee Chair Joe Gruters in the Oval Office at the White House, posted on Gruters' Instagram account. (Joe Gruters/Instagram)
Fox News Digital has also confirmed an AP report regarding Gruters' letter to RNC members last week, when he defended specific expenditures that have raised concerns among the party membership.

Nevada GOP Chair Michael McDonald told Fox News Digital that "it comes down to this. President Trump has made his choice. He's the leader of our party. This is who they want to go with, and we have to get behind our leaders and regroup."
McDonald praised Gruters for his "personal touch" and said, "KC's a dear friend, so I don't have anything bad to say about her."

But he added, "We have to focus on looking out and not looking in and having internal fights. So I hope everybody comes together on this and gets behind Joe ... we have to move this party forward behind what the president wants."

Longtime Iowa GOP chair Jeff Kaufmann praised Gruters for sending "some of the best RNC staffers and directors on the ground out here that I could ever hope for. The resources given to us were amazing."
And Kaufmann emphasized, "President Trump has unambiguously and very strongly endorsed Joe Gruters and that’s all I need."
SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

In the wake of the ballot box setbacks, no party-led autopsy appears to be in the works. And Crosbie, in her letter to committee members, pointed to the midterms and emphasized "we lost races in places we have long counted on. We owe ourselves an honest account of why."

"Voters were focused on the cost of living and the direction of the country. Our improvements in field operations, voter contact, and election-integrity infrastructure were valuable, but they did not answer those concerns or deliver the results we needed," she emphasized. "Some voters who supported us in 2024 stayed home or voted differently in 2026. We must ask whether we addressed the issues that mattered most to them, gave our candidates the support they needed, and nominated candidates who could win the races before them."

KC Crosbie, co-chair of the RNC, speaks during a Get Out the Vote rally hosted by the Republican Party of Kentucky in Lexington, Ky., on Saturday, October 24, 2026. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)
RNC member Oscar Brock of Tennessee, who is supporting Crosbie’s candidacy, told Fox News Digital "the goal of the national party is to elect Republicans and that’s true across the country."

"While we have traditionally deferred to the president to suggest who should be the national committee chairman, in this case we would hope the president would change his mind, because those of us who are supporting KC Crosbie for national chairman see Joe as having failed to do a successful job," Brock said.

Sue Cienki, an RNC committee member from Rhode Island, said KC is a member's member. She's done a great outreach the past couple of years" and added, "I don't think the members know Joe as well as they know KC.

We had a devastating loss on Election Day and I think people are looking for some sort of change," Cienki added. "It's not, in any way, shape or form, an insult to the president. I think that we're all in the 168 supportive of his policies, and we want to make sure the next two years go as smoothly for him as possible. But we are a separate entity from the White House."
But Gruters supporters highlighted his fundraising and organizational efforts.

RNC committee member from Maine Lauren LePage told Fox News Gruters was "incredibly responsive this cycle...he’s raised a ton of money for the party and supported candidates up and down the ballot ... although we suffered some losses, Chairman Gruters certainly did his job."

LePage, whose father, former two-term Maine Gov. Paul LePage, captured a Democrat-controlled open congressional seat in a rare midterm flip for the GOP, said that the RNC "made enormous investments in the ground game in Maine that resulted in a victory in CD 2."

Chair of the Republican National Committee Joe Gruters speaks during the RNC Winter Meeting at the Hilton Santa Barbara Beachfront Resort in Santa Barbara, California, on January 23, 2026. (Patrick T. Fallon / AFP via Getty Images)
In neighboring New Hampshire, RNC committee member Bill O'Brien pointed to Gruters and Crosbie and said, "I think there are two good candidates. I like them both."
But O'Brien, a former state House speaker, said, "2028 starts now, and Joe Gruters is the leader we need at the RNC to win."

"We need to build our war chest, strengthen our state parties, and protect the ballot. I’m proud to support Joe’s reelection as RNC chairman," O'Brien added. "We need proven leadership so we can fire on all cylinders and stay in the fight."
Another RNC committee member, who asked to remain anonymous to speak more freely, said "I’m with Joe. Nobody’s happy with the election, but it’s nothing against Joe. It’s nothing Joe could control."

"When your party has the White House, with all due respect to the chair, the RNC is an arm of the White House and so if people have a beef or a grievance, it’s with the White House, not with Joe. And so I think it would be unfair to hold Joe accountable," the committee member emphasized.
Since Trump's first election to the White House a decade ago, the RNC has experienced significant membership turnover, with those coming on board seen as loyal supporters of the president.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Former longtime RNC committee member from Mississippi Henry Barbour, who left the committee two years ago after serving for nearly two decades, told Fox News Digital, "Historically, anytime the White House has a candidate for RNC chair, they win, and I expect that Gruters will win."

"But I do think we need to have a discussion about the future of the party and what’s at stake and how do we get back on a winning path," Barbour added. "The only job of a political party is to win elections. That’s the number one job, and we’re failing at it."
Paul Steinhauser covers the national campaign trail from coast to coast for Fox News

title: China's Xi surprises Trump at tarmac, reciprocating gesture shown months ago
summary: Xi Jinping personally greeted Donald Trump at Shenzhen's airport, a rare welcome mirroring Trump's earlier tarmac reception and signaling reciprocity.
story: President Donald Trump lands in Shenzhen, China, for the APEC summit, where Chinese President Xi Jinping greets him on the tarmac with an elaborate welcome ceremony. Bill Melugin reports on the high-stakes arrival and national security analyst Dr. Rebecca Grant analyzes the diplomatic significance of the meeting.
President Donald Trump said he expected a special reception from China's Xi Jinping, and Wednesday morning's reception did not disappoint.

After Trump's in-person welcome of Xi at Joint Base Andrews in September, Xi personally greeted Trump at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport, a rare airport welcome ahead of a three-way meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Putin, who has met with Xi dozens of times and arrived at the same Shenzhen airport earlier Wednesday, did not receive a personal greeting from the Chinese leader. Instead, senior Chinese Communist Party advisor Cai Qi welcomed Putin upon arrival.
'RED CARPET FOR A DESPOT': TRUMP'S LAVISH XI WELCOME COLLIDES WITH GOP ANTI-COMMUNISM MESSAGE
Some Democratic and Republican lawmakers had criticized Trump over that September airport greeting, but it has brought Xi to reciprocate.

The Trump greeting marked a sharp contrast with Trump's previous visit to China in May, when Chinese Vice President Han Zheng met him at the airport in Beijing. Xi, who has led China for more than a decade, has rarely — if ever — appeared at an airport to welcome a visiting foreign leader, according to reports.
XI PRAISES US STATE VISIT 'PERFECTION' AS TRUMP CALLS MEETINGS 'VERY PRODUCTIVE'

President Donald Trump speaks with China's President Xi Jinping as he arrives at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province, on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. (Mark Schiefelbein - Pool/Getty Images)

As Trump stepped off Air Force One, a handshake between the two leaders turned into a brief hug while military regiments and performers dressed in pink and turquoise stood at attention. A military band played the U.S. and Chinese national anthems as dancers waved flowers, pompoms and American and Chinese flags.
U.S. President Donald Trump is greeted by China's President Xi Jinping at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport on Nov. 18, 2026, in Shenzhen, China. (Win McNamee/Getty Images)
"China is a nation that values courtesy and has a tradition of returning goodwill with goodwill," a report in China's Xinhua read.
REAL WINNER OF XI SUMMIT REVEALED AS TRUMP LOOKS TO USHER IN NEW ERA WITH CHINA
The leaders' exchange represents a new U.S.-China relationship of "respect, fairness, and reciprocity," Dean Wu Xinbo of Fudan University in Shanghai told The New York Times.
It showed China will "still treat him seriously and would like to continue to work with him," he added.
TRUMP SET FOR ECONOMIC SHOWDOWN WITH XI AS UNFULFILLED PROMISES LEAVE BILLIONS HANGING IN BALANCE
International Crisis Group senior analyst William Yang noted the gesture before potentially turbulent talks to come.

"It’s important to highlight the reciprocity that Xi gave to Trump by receiving him on the tarmac," Yang wrote Wednesday morning on X. "This gesture likely reflects Xi and Beijing’s desire to show respect to Trump, which they know the US President enjoys, and it is likely also an attempt to uphold the positive rapport between Xi and Trump ahead of a potentially turbulent period in U.S.-China relations in the coming months."
TRUMP ARRIVES IN PHILIPPINES AHEAD OF XI JINPING SUMMIT IN CHINA AFTER GOP MIDTERM LOSSES

Trump, Xi and Putin are in Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. The three leaders are scheduled to meet together Thursday on the sidelines of the economic gathering — an unprecedented three-way session.

Ahead of a one-on-one meeting with Xi on Wednesday, Putin said he expected "great potential benefits" from Thursday's three-way discussion. The session has drawn concern from officials in Ukraine, Iran and Taiwan, who worry the leaders of the world's three most powerful nations could make decisions affecting their futures without their participation.
During a briefing last week, a senior U.S. official said the three-way meeting is unlikely to produce any formal denuclearization agreement, calling it an "entry point" and "the first conversation."
Trump will meet Putin one-on-one tomorrow on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, a U.S. official confirmed to Fox News.
Earlier Wednesday morning, Trump recapped his trip to the Philippines.

"I am now heading to China, from the Philippines, where we had a wonderful meeting on Trade, National Security, and other subjects," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "I am pleased to announce that we made a new and completely different Trade Deal with the Philippines, one that will be a true landmark and, in particular, a Deal that will be great for our Farmers and those in the business of 'Energy.'
"President Marcos is a powerful leader, and a man of high integrity and substance. It was an Honor to be with him, and his beautiful wife and son. See you in China!"
Fox News' Lucas Tomlinson contributed to this report.

Eric Mack is a breaking news reporter and writer Sunday through Thursday, 6 a.m. ET to 2 p.m. ET, with a particular interest in stories that lead the news cycle on politics, elections, foreign affairs and government.

title: Trump-Xi showdown revives 25-year-old Clinton China 'mistake' as Senate vet demands reversal
summary: Former Trump ambassador Sam Brownback says it's time to reverse permanent normal trade relations with China, calling the 2000 decision a mistake.
story: President Donald Trump warned Iran on Monday that it would face unprecedented retaliation if it were to carry out an attack on Washington, D.C.

Former Trump Ambassador Sam Brownback is urging Washington to reverse a decades-old trade decision and strip China of its permanent normal trade relations status, arguing the United States must rethink its economic relationship with Beijing as President Donald Trump prepares to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

"I think it's time we back up and correct the mistake we made 25 years ago in granting normal trade relations with China, a country that seeks our demise and doesn't grant human rights, and remove that," Brownback told Fox News Digital in an interview.

Trump is traveling to China this week for his third meeting of the year with Xi, with the two leaders scheduled to hold talks Thursday in Shenzhen before joining Russian President Vladimir Putin for a trilateral meeting, amid ongoing trade tensions and concerns over American dependence on Chinese supplies.
TRUMP BRINGS TWO DIVIDED CABINET HEAVYWEIGHTS TO CHINA AS CONTROVERSY HANGS OVER HIGH-STAKES TALKS
"I think, tactically, President Trump is playing through this right," Brownback said. "But we're in a tough spot right now."

Brownback, who served as ambassador-at-large for international religious freedom during Trump's first administration, pointed to Washington's decision more than two decades ago to establish permanent normal trade relations with China.

President Bill Clinton signed legislation authorizing permanent normal trade relations with China in 2000, and President George W. Bush formally granted the trade status in December 2001, following China's accession to the World Trade Organization.
Revoking China's permanent normal trade relations status would generally subject Chinese imports to higher tariffs, rather than automatically ending trade between the two countries.
Brownback said that reducing those dependencies and restructuring trade relations would require years rather than an immediate break with Beijing.
TRUMP SHOULD PRESS XI ON CHINA’S PERSECUTION OF BELIEVERS AT HOME AND ABROAD
Chinese President Xi Jinping and President Donald Trump visit the Temple of Heaven on May 14, 2026, in Beijing, China. (Brendan Smialowski - Pool/Getty Images)
Brownback argued that the United States should now consider reversing that decision through an orderly process that would pressure Beijing to respect human rights and religious freedom.

He suggested reaching a "Helsinki Accords 2.0" deal, modeled on a landmark 1975 Cold War agreement that incorporated human rights into broader discussions between the United States, its European allies and the Soviet Union.
The agreement, Brownback said, would allow Washington to negotiate with Beijing over trade and religious freedom while warning that continued abuses could jeopardize normal trade relations.
"Either you grant human rights and religious freedom to your own people, or we're pulling back normal trade relations," Brownback said.

China's first lady Peng Liyuan, China's President Xi Jinping, President Donald Trump and first lady Melania Trump pose on the North Portico steps of the White House ahead of a state dinner in Washington, D.C., on Sept. 24, 2026. President Xi is on a state visit to the United States from Sept. 23 to 25. (SAUL LOEB/AFP via Getty Images)

Brownback also urged Trump to raise religious persecution directly with Xi, arguing that Beijing's treatment of Christians and other religious groups should become a central part of future negotiations.
THE CCP’S NEW ‘UNITY’ LAW TURNS CHINA’S REPRESSION INTO A GLOBAL THREAT

The U.S. Department of Labor estimated in 2022 that 100,000 Uyghurs and other ethnic minority former detainees in China may have been working under forced-labor conditions following detention in re-education camps.
"We can't trade with you if you're going to continue to operate the way you are, particularly towards people of faith, towards Christians," Brownback said.
Brownback said stabilizing the relationship would itself represent a meaningful achievement while the United States works to reduce its dependence on Chinese supplies.

"I think a successful trip is a continuation of the current situation right now, just stabilizing the relationship, not having it deteriorate further until we get in a better position on dealing with things like rare earth minerals and pharmaceutical supplies," Brownback said.
AMERICA DEPENDS TOO MUCH ON CHINA FOR ESSENTIAL MINERALS. WE NEED TO DIG OUR FUTURE
Sam Brownback urges reversing normal trade relations with China, citing human rights abuses and a long-term threat, as President Trump meets Xi Jinping. (Sarah Silbiger/Getty Images)
He also argued that religious freedom represents a strategic vulnerability for China's communist leadership, which he said views independent religious institutions as a threat to its authority.
