title: National security and AI figures urge DOJ to probe what Nvidia knew about chip smuggling
summary: A letter from 15 national security and AI leaders scrutinized the chipmaker’s knowledge of illegal transfers of its chips to China.
story: A group of 15 national security experts and AI policy leaders is urging the Justice Department to investigate what Nvidia knew about the alleged smuggling of its advanced AI chips to China,  and whether the company continued doing business with customers after evidence emerged that they were illegally diverting the technology.

The letter, sent Tuesday and addressed to Attorney General Todd Blanche, asks the department to examine whether Nvidia kept selling chips to customers or middlemen after receiving evidence that they were illegally routing them to China, or whether the company “deliberately blinded itself to export control violations.”

“The United States has the world’s most advanced SI chip technology, much of it built by Nvidia,” the letter states, using the Trump administration’s “super intelligence” label for AI. “Smuggling operations threaten to undermine that lead, giving China access to hardware necessary for developing advanced SI and deploying it to boost its military capabilities and international influence.”

The 15 signatories include a range of national security experts and AI policy specialists, such as David Buckley, the Central Intelligence Agency’s former inspector general; Randy Manner, a retired Army general; Chris McGuire, a former Biden official who specialized in chips; and Brad Carson, the president of Americans for Responsible Innovation, the AI advocacy group that organized the letter.

“China and our competitors around the world have their sights set on our advanced AI chips so they can build up their AI capabilities,” Carson told NBC News. “Nvidia’s advanced AI chips are at the top of their wish lists.”

Nvidia did not respond to a request for comment. On Tuesday, the company’s board of directors announced that it would establish a committee dedicated to investigating national security and export control compliance.

In a statement, a Justice Department spokesperson said: “As a general policy, the Department doesn’t discuss the details or existence of ongoing investigations, but it goes without saying that any investigation by the DOJ is based in evidence and facts.”

The letter comes amid growing scrutiny of the American chipmaker and calls from Congress to investigate the extent of Nvidia’s awareness of the chips’ destination and whether the company did anything about potential smuggling.

On Tuesday, the Justice and Commerce departments shared details about their investigation of Megaspeed, the Singaporean company tied to suspected Chinese intelligence asset Alice Huang. Nvidia’s former CEO Jensen Huang is alleged to have had an affair with Megaspeed’s Huang. Megaspeed reportedly acquired billions of dollars’ worth of Nvidia chips and is also being investigated over concerns that it — and its subsidiaries — smuggled chips to China.

In a joint statement Tuesday, the agencies said Commerce opened an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024, requested sales records from Nvidia in May 2025 and that Nvidia placed the company on its no-sell list the following month. Commerce investigators also conducted an in-person inspection of Megaspeed’s facilities with Singaporean law enforcement in June 2025.
A source familiar with the matter said that Nvidia itself is not the target of any existing investigation related to national security.

The Justice Department said it took the lead in the criminal investigation after that enforcement action. The agencies said they would continue working together to pursue any criminal conduct that may have occurred.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Huang has agreed to sit for an interview with several national security-focused House committees on Dec. 1, according to House Republicans. The appearance will focus on the former CEO’s role in “a potential breach of our national security,” according to the lawmakers.

Tuesday’s letter to Blanche points to several smuggling cases the Justice Department has brought in the past year involving Nvidia. In March 2026, prosecutors charged three people in an alleged scheme in which a Southeast Asian intermediary bought roughly $2.5 billion worth of servers containing advanced AI chips. Prosecutors allege at least $510 million worth were illegally sent to China.

“Repeated attempts to route Nvidia chips to China point to a pattern that warrants a closer examination of company practices and how Nvidia responded to repeated alarming discoveries over the past several years regarding the scale of smuggling operations,” the letter states.

Smuggled chips are estimated to equal at least 25% of the chips Chinese AI companies obtained through legal routes — though the actual figure may be far larger. Many Chinese companies, including tech titans Alibaba and Tencent, have reportedly also leased chips from data centers based in Singapore, Malaysia and other southeast Asian countries.

This week, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and the department’s Bureau of Industry and Security announced that it would close that loophole. The department said it would enact a new set of regulations limiting foreign data centers’ ability to rent their chips to Chinese companies and enacting new requirements for chip customers in five southeast Asian countries — including Singapore and Malaysia — in order to receive chips from American companies like Nvidia or AMD.

China criticized the rule. “Such actions run counter to the consensus reached between the two sides, infringe upon the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese enterprises, and disrupt the stability of global industrial and supply chains,” foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said at a regular briefing in Beijing.

Nvidia’s most advanced AI chips are widely considered the most powerful available. Under current export rules, Nvidia cannot sell its top-tier chips to China, though it can sell older generation chips, from the H200 family, to China with a 25% fee taken by the White House.

The Justice Department established a new body dedicated to cracking down on AI-related crime in early November. This force, called the Super Intelligence Task Force, aims to “ensure that America’s leadership in SI is not compromised by the misuse of SI by foreign state and state-sponsored actors, transnational criminal organizations, and individual or corporate actors engaged in fraud or other unlawful conduct,” according to the Department.

Some lawmakers have clamored for stricter rules on advanced AI chip exports to China. Members of the House’s Select Committee on China have sought to restrict China’s ability to purchase chipmaking equipment and to implement stronger chip-tracking technology — to ensure that chips sent to data centers outside mainland China remain outside of the country.
Tuesday’s letter closes by urging the department “to follow the evidence wherever it leads and pursue appropriate enforcement action where violations are established.”

title: Intense rain and flooding hits both U.S. coasts, causing major issues in Florida
summary: Florida’s east coast is being battered by heavy downpours as floodwaters rise in the southern part of the state, and the severe weather is expected to continue throughout the week.
story: Florida’s east coast is being battered by heavy downpours as floodwaters rise in the southern part of the state, and the severe weather is expected to continue throughout the week.

The rain started Tuesday in South Florida, with one round of heavy rain already in the Fort Lauderdale and Hollywood area. Radar estimates show 10 to 15 inches of rainfall, with rates as high as 3 inches per hour at times.

By Wednesday morning, the heavy rain was expected to continue. Another foot of rain is possible before the weekend, with rainfall rates of up to 3 inches per hour in some areas. On Wednesday morning, the city of Hollywood urged residents to shelter in place.
Around 11 million people from Miami to Jacksonville are at risk of flooding. In Melbourne, some waited in bumper-to-bumper traffic for hours to secure sandbags.
Generally, 4 to 6 inches of rain are expected, with totals expected to reach 8 to 12 inches, or higher, locally. Intense rainfall rates of 2 to 4 inches per hour are possible.
The St. Johns River is already at a major flood stage. Urban flash flooding and river flooding will be likely as the storm continues.

Broward County closed schools Wednesday, including before- and after-school care programs and extracurricular activities. The district has not yet announced whether schools will be closed at all later this week.
Miami-Dade Public Schools are staying open Wednesday, but the district said in a social media post that it would be flexible with tardiness due to the weather.
The roof of Temple Sinai in Hollywood partially collapsed, according to video from NBC 6 South Florida. And Memorial Regional Hospital, also in Hollywood, suspended visitation for the day.
Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport issued a ground stop around 9:30 a.m. Wednesday, and it was expected to stay in effect until at least 10:45 a.m.
The latest batch of rains come just weeks after the region saw a 1- in-1,000-year rain event that similarly brought heavy rain and flooding.
“I think everyone learned their lesson,” Christian Greene told NBC News. “No one wants to do that again.”
For Subscribers

Videos from Hollywood show cars stuck and submerged — with some people abandoning their vehicles in the mess. Water was seen rushing through neighborhoods elsewhere, and residents were forced to drive through floods overnight. An NBC News-verified social media video shows hail falling in Fort Lauderdale on Tuesday night.
Maj. Jason Drinkwater with the Brevard County Sheriff’s Office called the preparations “precautionary.”
“People are losing their homes. They’re losing a lot of their personal belongings in their homes, and obviously they want to protect that,” Drinkwater said.
Threat of dangerous waves
Heavy rains and gusty winds are hitting northern California this morning, from Redding to San Francisco, and heavy rain will spread south throughout Wednesday.
Winter weather alerts are in place for 1 million people, 12 million are under flood alerts and 9 million are facing wind alerts.
Dangerous waves, flooding and strong winds are expected, along with power outages.
Both Los Angeles and the Bay Area could see 1 to 3 inches of rain locally, with 3 to 5 inches in the mountains. Rates of 3 inches per hour are expected.
For Subscribers
The soaking rain will move through California om Wednesday, with an elevated flood risk along the coast.
The Sierra Nevada is also facing the potential for some heavy snow this week, with up to 4 feet expected on the mountain passes. Heavy snow will blanket the Sierra into tonight.
On Thursday, the storm will move east, bringing rain and snow to the Great Basin region, while snow continues over the Sierra Nevada.

title: They were NFL losers last year. Now they’re playoff contenders.
summary: The Cleveland Browns, Cincinatti Bengals, Kansas City Chiefs, New York Giants, Detroit Lions and Minnesota Vikings all missed the 2025 playoffs, but now make up nearly half of this season’s projected postseason field.
story: If you haven’t been paying much attention to the NFL, this season’s projected playoff field might look unrecognizable.
Cleveland? Cincinnati? Kansas City? The New York Giants?

One year ago, each endured a brutal 2025 season that left them with six or fewer wins and watching the playoffs from home. Fast-forward to this fall, when after 10 weeks, they’ve already won more games than they did all of last year.
Those turnarounds have put them in the driver’s seat for the upcoming playoffs — and they’re not alone in going from missing out to becoming a postseason factor.
Both Detroit and Minnesota missed the NFC’s final playoff spot last season while finishing 9-8 in a brutally difficult NFC North. Now, both are 7-2.

The NFL’s postseason includes 14 teams; if the current playoff projections were to hold, the Browns, Bengals, Chiefs, Giants, Lions and Vikings would make up nearly half the field only 12 months after failing to make the last postseason. Their revival is a reminder of how quickly franchises’ fortunes can change.

Their quick turnarounds don’t owe to a few shared traits. Each ranks in the league’s upper half in fewest points allowed. Most draw around the league average in penalties and create around the league average in turnovers.

The biggest catalyst for the Giants’ (5-3-1) switch from the bottom of the NFC East to its top took place when they hired longtime coach John Harbaugh in the offseason. Yet all of their months of planning for a new era were upended in only Week 2, when starting quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending knee injury.

New York patched together the position before taking a leap of faith and trading for J.J. McCarthy, a 2024 first-round pick who had quickly lost the Vikings’ confidence. In New York, McCarthy hasn’t turned into an overnight passing sensation in his four games as starter, with only two touchdowns and two interceptions. Still, his rating and completion percentage are better than the Giants’ previous backup, which in the middling NFC East has kept the Giants in first place.

By leading the NFL in blitzes and pressure — including eight sacks in Sunday’s key win against NFC North rival Green Bay — Minnesota’s defense has kept the team competitive all season and has provided a high floor for their potential.
Their playoff ceiling will be determined by their offense, however.
“All we have to do is be mediocre at this point,” star receiver Justin Jefferson said Sunday.

title: Xi greets Trump as he arrives in China, a rare move ahead of Putin talks
summary: In a rare and surprising move, Chinese leader Xi Jinping personally greeted President Donald Trump as he arrived in China on Wednesday ahead of historic three-way talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
story: SHENZHEN, China — In a rare and surprising move, Chinese leader Xi Jinping personally greeted President Donald Trump as he arrived in China on Wednesday ahead of historic three-way talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
It is believed to be the first time that Xi, in power for more than a decade, has been on hand to greet any foreign leader arriving in China.

He was reciprocating the personal greeting he had received from Trump in September, when the American leader met him at the plane upon his arrival for a White House state visit. Lawmakers from both parties had criticized Trump over the move, which is also rare for U.S. presidents.

A report by Xinhua, China’s state-run news agency, said that during Trump’s arrival in the city of Shenzhen on Wednesday, Xi noted the special trip the American president and first lady Melania Trump had made to welcome him at Joint Base Andrews outside Washington.
“China is a nation that values courtesy and has a tradition of returning goodwill with goodwill,” the Xinhua report said.

After Trump descended from Air Force One, a handshake between the two leaders turned into a quick hug as rows of military regiments and performers wearing bright pink and turquoise outfits stood at attention. A martial band played the American and Chinese national anthems as dancers waved flowers, pompoms and Chinese and American flags.

title: House Democrat warns a dozen Trump allies to save their records, calling it ‘just the beginning’
summary: Democratic Rep. Robert Garcia, who will chair the House Oversight Committee, sent 12 letters to associates of President Donald Trump to save their records ahead of investigations.
story: WASHINGTON — The highest-ranking Democrat on the House Oversight Committee sent a dozen letters to associates of President Donald Trump on Wednesday telling them to save their records ahead of the Democratic takeover of Congress in January.

The letters from Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., who is expected to chair the Oversight Committee when Democrats take control of the House early next year, were addressed to administration officials, as well as members of Trump’s family, and focus on allegations of corruption, as well as the administration’s handling of the Jeffrey Epstein files.

“Oversight Democrats are fighting to put an end to this Administration’s self-dealing, misconduct, and abuse,” Garcia said in a statement. “These investigations will lay the groundwork for legislation which helps all Americans. This is just the beginning.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

The preservation letters offered a preview of some of the committee’s priorities come January. Garcia’s team sent letters to Trump’s sons Donald Trump, Jr. and Eric Trump, as well as Trump Jr.’s ex-fiancé and former ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle. Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner also received a letter about his investments in the Middle East.

Letters were sent to several current and former administration officials: Vice President JD Vance, White House chief of staff Stephen Miller, former White House chief of staff Susie Wiles, Attorney General Todd Blanche, former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem and former DHS senior adviser Corey Lewandowski.

The CEO of the Trust for the National Mall, Catherine Townsend, received a letter focused on the construction of the White House ballroom using both public funds and donations from private entities, including corporations with business before the government. The trust, a nonprofit, is collecting donations for the project, including from no-public donors.

Two Federal Bureau of Prisons officials — BOP Director William K. Marshall III and Federal Prison Camp Bryan Prison Warden Tanisha Hall — also received a letter about the transfer of Epstein’s co-conspirator Ghislaine Maxwell to a minimum-security prison camp. (Maxwell was convicted on federal sex trafficking charges for her role in recruiting teenage girls to have sex with Epstein, the late financier and convicted sex offender.)
The White House said that Trump is “willing to work with anyone to continue delivering victories for hardworking Americans.”
“If Democrats choose to pursue sham investigations and radical left policies, they are choosing to work against the American people,” said Lauren Bis, a White House spokeswoman.

Garcia is one of four Democratic members of Congress who have already been targeted by U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of Texas Aaron Reitz, a Trump administration official who has quickly made himself the face of aggressive pushback on Democrats as they prepare for public oversight. Reitz wrote his own preservation letter to Garcia, as well as Sens. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., and Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., and posted them on X, saying he was conducting a “preliminary investigation” into the speech of Democratic members of Congress.

Reitz’s unusual letters, which cite two federal civil rights statutes, have received significant criticism from legal experts and mark a departure from Justice Department traditions. An outside nonprofit group has filed an ethics complaint against Reitz over the letters.

Reitz told NBC News that he was in “constant contact” with Justice Department leaders and that the letters were the result of his “organic conversations” with senior leadership at the DOJ. He  said he was “not interested in chilling free speech” but wanted to discourage people from breaking federal law.

White House counsel Will Scharf also sent a letter to Garcia last month warning that the Trump administration was “monitoring” the speech of Democratic members of Congress as they plan investigations into the Trump administration, saying that “threats to executive branch officials designed to deter them from public service, or process designed merely to abuse or instill fear in the recipient may cross the line into blatant criminality.”

The Supreme Court has said that congressional investigations must have a valid legislative purpose. In addition to their First Amendment rights, members of Congress have their rights protected by the speech or debate clause of the U.S. Constitution, which provides legislators with immunity from prosecution for their official actions.

title: Jeff Bezos says he was ‘heavily involved’ in picking the new James Bond
summary: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos told an audience that he was “heavily involved” with casting Robert Pattinson to play the new James Bond, saying that  he displayed “something special.”
story: Tech billionaire and Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has said that he was “heavily involved” with casting the new James Bond, telling  an audience on Tuesday night that actor Robert Pattinson had displayed “something special.”
Amazon MGM Studios assumed creative control of the blockbuster franchise last year, tapping Denis Villeneuve to direct its first instalment.
In a rare peek into the casting of the iconic British spy, Bezos pulled back the curtain on the selection process that ultimately saw Pattinson announced as 007 to much global fanfare on Monday.
“We ran a really tight process and we made the final decision on Friday,” Bezos told Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World event in California.

A “big group” of contenders were whittled down to five finalists who went through “real, old-fashioned screen tests” Bezos said. He added that the contenders each acted out three different scenes with “full costume, real sets, other actors with them,” to help with the casting process.
Bezos did not name the finalists, but actors who reportedly tested for the role included Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor, Jack Lowden and Nicholas Hoult.
Bezos said that he and a team, including the movie’s director Villeneuve, spent hours reviewing the finalists on Friday, noting that they were all “extraordinarily talented.”
But he said “there was something special about Rob and his performances ... It was immediately un-debated,” he added. “We all gravitated toward Rob.”
Pattinson said playing the suave British spy was “the honour of a lifetime.” In a statement on Monday, he added, “to say this role is a dream come true is an understatement.”
With a career spanning more than two decades, Pattinson took to the screen as a teenager playing vampire Edward Cullen in the “Twilight” movies and Cedric Diggory in the “Harry Potter” franchise.
A distinctive and versatile actor, he went on to pivot between smaller independent films and mega-studio productions including “The Batman.”

Pattinson also recently enjoyed a viral turn as villainous Antinous in Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster “The Odyssey,” and played a shapeshifting assassin in “Dune: Part Three,” which saw him work with director Villeneuve.
The script for the new Bond film is being written by Steven Knight, who created the British television series “Peaky Blinders.” No release date has yet been given for the new movie.
Bond has evolved into one of the most coveted and discussed roles in film, with the book-to-screen character written by Ian Fleming displaying rare staying power across generations.

“I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey ... but there can only be one 007,” director Villeneuve said in a statement this week. “I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new.”

The six previous Bond actors — Sean Connery, George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan and Daniel Craig — were little-known or drawn primarily from stage and small-screen work before being catapulted into fame as the secret agent.
Bezos said initially the casting team had been “slightly biased” against Pattinson because he is “already so famous” and said they had been seeking “somebody a little more unknown.”
Ultimately, he added, “in the screening tests, it was so obvious, he is James Bond.”

title: Amid string of outages, bipartisan letter urges strategy to combat AI-assisted cyber threats
summary: In the midst of a series of recent cyber outages, there is growing concern by members of Congress that the Trump administration needs to do more to protect infrastructure from cyberattacks that are aided by AI, according to a new bipartisan letter sent by two senators to the White House’s AI czar.
story: In the midst of a series of recent cyber outages, there is growing concern by members of Congress that the Trump administration needs to do more to protect infrastructure from cyberattacks that are aided by AI, according to a new bipartisan letter sent by two senators to the White House’s AI czar.

The letter from U.S. Sens. Maria Cantwell from Washington state, the top Democrat on the Senate Commerce Committee, and Mike Rounds, the Republican from South Dakota who chairs the Senate Armed Services Committee Subcommittee on Cybersecurity, urges AI czar Jay Clayton to develop a new national strategy that addresses AI-assisted cyber threats.
“AI is rapidly increasing the ability to discover and exploit weaknesses in software, and our defenses are not keeping pace,” the senators wrote.

They noted that AI can quickly find vulnerabilities in software and get around regular cyber defenses. Repair patches that are supposed to protect infrastructure can take weeks or months to test and install. And they wrote that autonomous AI agents can introduce new security risks.
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment Tuesday.

It’s not clear what kind of role, if any, AI has played in the ongoing outages impacting U.S. consumers and travelers, but questions are expected to come up when Clayton testifies before the House Committee on Homeland Security on Wednesday morning.

Clayton who also serves as the Director of National Intelligence was named to the AI role in early October is leading a task force of government officials to produce an AI policy by the end of January.
For Subscribers

In their letter to Clayton, the senators cited an ongoing wave of cyberattacks in Japan that have impacted financial institutions and companies, leading “to large-scale data breaches and leaks, which the Japanese government is now seeking to contain.” The string of attacks are believed to be boosted by AI.
For Subscribers
They also pointed to incidents where rogue artificial intelligence agents have accessed customers’ bank accounts, leaving banks worried that AI could initiate transactions on its own.
The senators are asking for Clayton’s task force to bring together AI companies and federal agencies to secure digital infrastructure and develop security standards for autonomous AI agents.

Speaking to reporters in the Philippines overnight, Secretary of State Marco Rubio sought to reassure Americans, saying that recent outages such as those that impacted Microsoft Outlook, United Airlines and the Federal Aviation Administration are not connected to one another.

“We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber hackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind,” he said.

title: Apple’s newest smartwatch is $70 off — just 2 months after launch
summary: The Apple Watch Series 12, the brand’s newest smartwatch, is already on sale. It’s a great upgrade for anyone who wants detailed health tracking and faster charging.
story: In the spirit of Black Friday and Cyber Monday, the Apple Watch Series 12 is up to $70 off on Amazon, bringing the 42mm GPS model down to its lowest price ever. That’s a pretty rare drop for a smartwatch that just came out in September, and it’s the Series 12’s first major discount since launch.

The Apple Watch has consistently been one of the best fitness trackers we’ve tested here at NBC Selected, with the previous Series 11 being the best smartwatch for anyone with an iPhone. So if you’ve been waiting to upgrade an older Apple Watch, or you want a holiday gift for someone that tracks their health around the clock, keep reading to find out more about this deal and why you won’t want to wait to grab it.
Apple Watch Series 12 (42mm, GPS)

The Series 12 is Apple’s newest flagship smartwatch, and its biggest upgrade is a redesigned Health Sensing System powered by the new S11 chip. It checks your heart rate in the background every five seconds and measures heart rate variability far more often than the Series 11, according to Apple. NBC Selected senior editor Shalwah Evans — who’s currently testing the Series 12 — bought the previous watch for her sister to monitor her heart rate and other health stats. “It’s easy to set up and sync. I just love that it gives me peace of mind that if something is off with her heart health, she has a tool that can send her an alert and do an ECG,” she says.

But if you ever feel too inundated with tons of biometric data, I like that the watch combines your activity and sleep into an easy-to-read “readiness score” each morning, so you have some foundational information about how hard to push yourself that day. Unlike Oura and Whoop, Apple doesn’t charge a subscription for Readiness or its other health features.

Battery life still tops out at 24 hours of normal use, but thankfully charging has gotten much faster: 15 minutes on the charger adds up to 12 hours of use, 50% more than the Series 11. If you’re hitting the trail or completing an outdoor workout, that uses up to 10 hours of battery. You also get new Siri features, including Live Rewind, which replays the last 15 seconds of any audio you missed. (Note: This is a feature you have to enable, it’s not automatic.)

While the discount may not seem like a lot compared to deals we typically feature (for comparison, the Apple Watch SE 3 is currently 20% off), it’s a surprising sale considering the smartwatch just launched this fall. The price might drop further when Black Friday officially arrives, it might not (or it could sell out before that). If it’s been on your radar as a purchase for the holidays, now’s the time to grab it.
Apple Watch Series 12 (46mm, GPS)
The 46mm model has the same features in a larger case with a bigger display, which makes texts and workout stats easier to read at a glance. It’s down to $379 from $429, also its lowest price ever.

As someone who owns a Series 11, I’d still say the upgrade is modest. The Series 12 makes the most sense if you’re coming from a Series 9 or older, or looking to gift someone their very first Apple Watch.

title: Gas geyser and noxious odor from L.A. area landfill prompts public health response
summary: Pungent odors wafting from the Chiquita Canyon Landfill prompted Los Angeles County officials to relocate residents after drilling unleashed a geyser of trash and fumes.
story: Pungent odors wafting from the Chiquita Canyon Landfill prompted Los Angeles County officials to order the company responsible to pay to relocate nearby residents after a drilling issue unleashed a geyser of trash and fumes.

Members of the fire department responded to the landfill Monday afternoon after a drill released gas into the air. The incident caused a plume of what appeared to be thick black smoke to rise, though it later turned white, according to NBC Los Angeles.
A “routine” operation was being done to install a new gas well to help with elevated temperatures, according to a statement Tuesday from Waste Connections, which owns and operates the site.
A pressurized pocket within the landfill was affected in the process, it said.
“This resulted in an above-ground release of gases and particulate material at the drilling location,” the company said. “No liquids were released, and no injuries have been reported.”
Drilling stopped and four people were taken to the hospital for evaluation, but Waste Connections said that no injuries have been reported.

The company is conducting air monitoring at the site as well as the local community. There were no indications that there was an excess of chemicals from based on California’s Reference Exposure Levels, the statement said.
“Chiquita continues to coordinate with state and local regulatory agencies and emergency response personnel,” Waste Connections said.

Los Angeles County’s public health department issued an emergency order Tuesday to have Waste Connections and Chiquita Canyon, LLC, provide immediate relief to the surrounding communities that are exposed to the “noxious odors.”

The order instructs the companies to provide residents with indoor spaces meant to provide relief from the odors, to provide short-term hotel stays for the immediate relocation of residents, and transportation for those who require assistance to reach those places.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
It also ordered that residents be provided support to improve their indoor air quality, such as air filters or purifiers.
Chiquita Canyon Landfill “has an obligation to timely and immediately provide relief to mitigate the exposures in the community,” the order said.

The work that was being done at the landfill was part of an Environmental Protection Agency order to properly handle the waste and mitigate odors at the landfill. The agency said that the landfill has seen a “significant subsurface elevated temperature event” since around May 2022.
The order included directives to redirect offgas by the end of this month.
Los Angeles County Supervisor Kathryn Barger described the “explosion and methane plume” as “unacceptable” in a post on X Monday night.
“I will be demanding answers and accountability,” Barger wrote.

title: Waymo pauses all robotaxi rides on U.S. freeways after California ban
summary: Waymo will stop putting its driverless vehicles on U.S. freeways for now.
story: Waymo will stop putting its driverless vehicles on U.S. freeways for now. The move comes after California banned the company’s robotaxis from state highways after officials determined that they pose an “imminent hazard to public safety.”

“We’ve proactively implemented a freeway operating restriction across all of our markets,” a Waymo spokesperson said Tuesday in a statement. “Notably, this only extends to our freeway service, and we’re working to quickly and safely re-open freeway routing.”

California’s Department of Motor Vehicles said it issued its ban Nov. 11 after one of Waymo’s autonomous vehicles tried to pass highway patrol officers conducting a traffic break on a San Francisco-area freeway this month.
The department also cited a separate incident in which three of the company’s vehicles entered an active construction closure on another San Francisco-area highway.

“The Department determined that Waymo’s driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present,” the department said.
Similar restrictions were placed on the company after similar incidents earlier this year, the department said.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
The ban will remain in place until Waymo can address the issue, according to the release.
In a statement, Waymo pointed out that the construction zone incidents did not involve injuries or collisions and said it is complying with the restrictions.
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said it is in communication with both the state DMV and Waymo and will “take additional actions as appropriate.”
Waymo’s robotaxis are in more than a dozen cities across the U.S. Waymo, which is owned by Google’s parent company, Alphabet Inc., first introduced the driverless taxis in San Francisco in 2024.
Waymo said it is working with state officials to “diligently and responsibly” resume freeway operations and service continues to operate normally on regular ground-level roads.

title: Druski Manifested His Comedy Success in a 2018 Tweet. He Reveals His Next Big Goal on TODAY
summary: Druski tweeted in 2018 his goal to be one of the biggest comedians in the world. Eight years later, he reveals his next lofty goal on TODAY.
story: Druski spoke his success into existence.

Before he landed a Netflix deal and before he became the youngest person to host the BET Awards and the first content creator to host “Saturday Night Live,” the 32-year-old posted a tweet back in 2018 about his ambitions.
“I will be 1 of the Biggest Comedians in the World .......,” he said.
The comedian, whose real name is Drew Desbordes, spoke to Craig Melvin, Al Roker and Dylan Dreyer on TODAY Nov. 18 about what prompted him to post that tweet.

“I’m big on manifesting,” he said. “I’ve always been one of those big believers that I write things down, and they come true. In that moment, I was very serious about that, and I was adamant, and I made it happen, so I’m grateful.”

Druski is coming off an “SNL” appearance that gave the show its highest rating in two years. His latest achievement is the upcoming release of his first Netflix special, a semi-scripted comedy series called “Collect & Praise” that drops on Dec. 1. Druski plays a money-hungry megachurch pastor with comedian Mike Epps as his scheming deacon in a series that Druski said was shot in less than two weeks.
He’s also appearing in his first movie role in 2027 in “The Catch,” an upcoming baseball romantic comedy starring Oscar winner Emma Stone and directed by Stone’s husband, Dave McCary.

“It was the first time in a long time I felt like a student again,” Druski said. “Being around just great actors and how good they are, watching how prepare and the small things they do, I’m just trying to learn.”
The experience also has him ready to manifest another lofty goal by speaking it out loud.
“Oh man, Oscar,” he said. “I got to get that Oscar! It’s on the way.”
He made the TODAY hosts echo his sentiment to help put it out into the universe. Al went a step further and said Druski is on his way to the coveted Oscar, Grammy, Tony and Emmy award superfecta.
“Druski, Oscar,” Al said. “Beginning of the EGOT.”
“Now we talking,” Druski said.

title: I Study James Bond for a Living. Here’s How I Reacted to the Robert Pattinson Casting (and Who I Would’ve Picked)
summary: What do James Bond experts think of Robert Pattinson’s casting?
story: “Take it From Me” is a TODAY series where experts use their wisdom to explain trends or make recommendations within their fields. In this, James Bond scholars weigh in on Robert Pattinson’s casting.
James Bond fans who waited seven long years to find out which actor would be the next to play the iconic British spy have gotten their answer.
Pattinson, Robert Pattinson.
Amazon MGM, which owns the rights to the Bond films, announced the choice on Nov. 16, which predictably left longtime fans either shaken or stirred.

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos revealed that he was involved in the decision at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World event in California. “We ran a really tight process and we made the final decision on Friday,” Bezos said, per NBC News reporting.

He added that there was a “big group” of actors who did “real, old-fashioned screen tests” to compete for the role. “There was something special about Rob and his performances,” Bezos said. “It was immediately un-debated. We all gravitated toward Rob.”

The 40-year-old star of “The Batman” and “The Odyssey” will succeed Daniel Craig, whose last Bond film was released in 2021. If the next Bond film is not released until 2028, it will have been the longest hiatus between movies in the franchise’s 64-year history, so the fans are thirsty for a new version.
TODAY.com discussed the casting choice with a trio of Bond scholars:

Oliver Buckton, the author of the Ian Fleming biography “The World Is Not Enough” and a professor and chair of the Department of English at Florida Atlantic UniversityColin Burnett, program director of Film & Media Studies at Washington University in St. Louis, and author of the forthcoming book “James Bond and the Art of Franchise Storytelling”James Chapman, the author of “Licence to Thrill: A Cultural History of the James Bond Films.”
Oliver Buckton, the author of the Ian Fleming biography “The World Is Not Enough” and a professor and chair of the Department of English at Florida Atlantic University
Colin Burnett, program director of Film & Media Studies at Washington University in St. Louis, and author of the forthcoming book “James Bond and the Art of Franchise Storytelling”
James Chapman, the author of “Licence to Thrill: A Cultural History of the James Bond Films.”
Here’s what they had to say.
A ‘Surprise’ Casting
Pattinson came on late as a candidate after it was previously reported that actors Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor, Jack Lowden and Nicholas Hoult had all undergone screen tests for the role in October.

“I was surprised, to be honest,” Buckton tells TODAY.com. “I think like a lot of people, we had in mind a shortlist that didn’t include him. But having time to think about it, it does make sense in a number of ways.”
“My immediate reaction was, ‘Wow, I wasn’t really expecting that,’ and then I got really excited about the idea,” Chapman says.
“At no point in history has a major A-list star been cast as James Bond at the peak of their career.”
Colin Burnett said on what makes Pattinson's casting remarkable
Burnett called Pattinson’s casting “a tectonic shift” in the way the role has been filled in the past.

“At no point in history has a major A-list star been cast as James Bond at the peak of their career,” Burnett says. “They have had reasonable careers, but Pattinson is someone who comes in aware of his stardom, of his box office potential, of his performance, and who’s very much going to look forward to steering the franchise. None of the previous actors had the clout on the way in to do that.”
Why Robert Pattinson’s Casting Makes Sense
The recurring theme that came up as to why Pattinson got the nod is simple: box office dollars.

Amazon MGM Studios took creative control of the Bond franchise in 2025 after making a deal with the franchise’s longtime producers, Michael G. Wilson and Barbara Broccoli. The change came four years after Amazon bought MGM, which owned the rights to the James Bond films, for $8.5 billion.

The online retail giant did not pay all that money to have the next Bond film to flop at the box office. That made going the traditional Bond route of casting an up-and-coming actor who is not yet widely known to the public, like Craig and former Bond actors Timothy Dalton and Pierce Brosnan, a gamble.

“I think that there’s so much at stake in this casting decision now with Amazon taking over and relaunching the whole franchise in a different way that they didn’t want to take a risk on an actor who hasn’t been in major films,” Buckton says.

“I know for a fact, having spoken to people inside Amazon, that they are hoping for and building the structure of Amazon MGM off a massive box office success (with Bond),” Burnett says. “What they’re hoping is to have a big hit right from the get-go, so that too is a major shift.”
Does Robert Pattinson Look the Part?

At 40, Pattinson is about the right age to play the superspy, who is generally considered to be in his late 30s, 40-ish in the Ian Fleming novels that made the character famous. The oldest actor to be cast as Bond was Roger Moore, who was 45 at the time.

Pattinson is also tall, lithe and dark-haired, which is closer to Fleming’s description of the character than Craig, who initially dealt with a wave of backlash about being blonde, short and muscular when he was first cast.
“People will feel just because of Pattinson’s look in a tuxedo with his hair back that he is James Bond, much more so than Daniel Craig,” Burnett says.
In an eerie coincidence, Pattinson resembles a cartoon rendering of Bond that Fleming had made in the late 1950s when he had a comic strip done of the character, according to Buckton.
“Fleming’s model was the 1930s star Hoagy Carmichael, but it looks uncannily like Robert Pattinson,” Buckton says.
Is Robert Pattinson Too Famous to Play Bond?
Will fans see James Bond on the screen or Robert Pattinson?

That is a question that has not been a problem for the six previous Bond actors, including the legendary Sean Connery, because they were not household names when they landed the role. The role made them famous.

“That’s the risk they’re taking, that he has too much baggage from other films,” Buckton says. “But he’s such a chameleon. Look at all the different roles he’s played, from ‘Twilight’ to ‘The Batman’ to movies like ‘The Lighthouse.’ I think they’re counting on him being able to do that again and reinvent himself as James Bond, and the fans will accept that.”
“The thing with Robert Pattinson is he changes with the times,” Burnett says. “He’s constantly reinventing himself.”

His experience in carrying big-budget films could actually be an asset rather than a drawback, according to the experts. It helps that he has already worked with director Denis Villeneuve on the “Dune” films because Villeneuve has committed to directing the next Bond film.

“He’s got that kind of crossover aspect to him,” Chapman says. “He’s done big franchise properties, big successful films with a female fanbase, so there’s real acting credentials there. He’s not a one-note actor. I’m thinking he can play Bond in a different way than he plays Batman.”
However, there’s also the possibility of overexposure if he’s also appearing in “Batman” and “Dune” movies in the midst of “Bond” films.

“Some of the negative reaction has been, let’s not have one actor taking on these iconic roles at the same time,” Buckton says. “That’s the risk, that Bond fans are like, ‘We want our own guy.  We want someone who’s not already Superman or Batman or whatever.’”
What Robert Pattinson Could Bring to the Role
Each of the previous six actors brought their own touch to the role, from the suave and sly Sean Connery to the campy Roger Moore to the brooding Daniel Craig.
Pattinson leaned in to a dark portrayal of Batman, so it remains to be seen how he balances the humor, physical prowess and romantic banter with the Bond girls in the new film.

“(Craig) became this wounded, dark, introspective James Bond, and I thought the new Bond would have to be a bit lighter,” Buckton says. “Even though (Pattinson) has played some dark characters, I think he has enough versatility. I would expect a little bit of a throwback to more of a suave, calm-under-pressure James Bond, and maybe a bit more of the Bond girl chemistry, which wasn’t Daniel Craig’s strong suit.”
“If Pattinson had come around and there had been no Craig, it would have been no problem to play more of a dark, psychological version, but Craig has cleared this ground already,” Burnett says.
Buckton speculated that maybe Pattinson’s performance in the Christopher Nolan movie “Tenet” could be a hint at what he does with Bond.
“I think that’s a glimpse of what he might be like because there’s something kind of edgy about him that I like, and maybe that’s what made him the choice,” he said.
Who Would Bond Experts Have Chosen?
Buckton liked “Superman” star Henry Cavill, 43, who was in the running for the role in the early 2000s as a 22-year-old but lost out to Craig.
Buckton would’ve gone with Callum Turner this time around.

“I could see him as Bond,” he says of Turner. “Some people say he didn’t have the charisma, but that’s something you can grow into. He could be identified as James Bond because he’s not a huge star right now, and I think he could bring that humor and a lighter touch to the role.”
Burnett would’ve gone with “Frankenstein” and “Wuthering Heights” star Jacob Elordi.

“I saw ‘Wuthering Heights’ in the theater and there’s a scene where he reemerges onscreen and the theater just swooned,” Burnett says. “That’s a star. That’s a thing Bond has always had. Men want to be like him and women want to be with him. Elordi has that feel.”

title: Walker Scobell Calls ‘Percy Jackson’ Season 3 ‘Most Accurate’ to the Books Yet
summary: Walker Scobell previews Season 3 of Disney+’s “Percy Jackson and the Olympians,” which will follow the events of “The Titan’s Curse” and majorly up the stakes.
story: Walker Scobell is ready for “The Titan’s Curse.” Percy Jackson, on the other hand, may not be.
“Be prepared,” Scobell tells TODAY.com. “It’s not like the other seasons... everything is a very real threat.”
With book and series fans alike anticipating Season 3 of “Percy Jackson and The Olympians,” set to release Nov. 20, the cast alludes to it as the series’ “darkest” addition yet.

Season 3 will follow the events of third book, “The Titan’s Curse.” With executive oversight by the series’ author, Rick Riordan, this will be the first time the third book has been adapted for the screen.

Riordan has been “involved in every writers room,” he told The Hollywood Reporter, much to the enthusiasm of book purists who were left disappointed by major changes in the Percy Jackson movie adaptations.

But Riordan isn’t the only one holding the TV adaptation to the book’s high standards. Scobell views the story from the perspective of its titular star and as a boy who first fell in love with the series at 9 years old.
“I would say it’s the most accurate season we’ve had, which was great for me,” Scobell tells TODAY.com.
To the 17-year-old, the more book-accurate the script is, the better.
“I almost sometimes wish I hadn’t read the books because, unfortunately, it’s hard for me to let it go,” he says.
“You know, there are things that have to change for (the show) to work,” he adds. “There’s also things that they’ve changed that have made it 10 times better.”
Previewing Season 3

“Percy Jackson and The Olympians” Season 3 will see Percy and an unlikely group of new characters journey across the country to find Annabeth (Leah Sava Jefferies) after she’s captured during their initial mission. Meanwhile, the threat of the demigod Luke (Charlie Bushnell), an impending war between the gods and titans and the great prophecy looms over Percy, who’s having to handle it all without Annabeth for the first time.
Like in previous seasons, this means viewers are in for plenty of epic showdowns — and on a grander scale than book readers may have originally envisioned, Scobell says.
“There are things we filmed that I was like, ‘Wow, this is so much bigger than it was in the books!’” he says.

It will also introduce some complicated new character dynamics, picking up with the cliffhanger at the end of Season 2. Thalia (Tamara Smart), the lost demigod daughter of Zeus, has returned to her human form after being turned into a tree years ago. This means that the great prophecy — which foretells that Olympus will be either saved or destroyed by a child of the big three gods (Zeus, Poseidon and Hades) — may not apply to Percy after all.

In the books, Percy and Thalia slowly establish a friendship, approaching each other with hesitancy but agreeableness. They also bond over the shared goal of saving Annabeth. But Scobell says that dynamic will look slightly different in Season 3, a change he says “works better” for the story’s arc.
“The only thing running through Percy’s head, in every single chapter in the book (is) ‘Annabeth, Annabeth, Annabeth,’” Scobell says.
In the show, Scobell’s character is driven by that same motivation, but the addition of Thalia adds “another level” of stakes to the quest.

“Now there’s this other girl, Thalia, who he doesn’t completely trust because they are so similar,” he adds. “It’s almost like he has to constantly choose what to focus on ... this ‘great prophecy’ with Thalia, or Annabeth.”
“I’m not going to spoil anything, but being so angry and intense at the beginning kind of carves out a nice story for the two of them,” he adds.

Thalia isn’t the only big three demigod Percy is going to have to look out for. “The Titan’s Curse” also famously introduces the di Angelo siblings, Bianca and Nico, to be played by Olive Abercrombie and and Levi Chrisopulos in Season 3. Fans of the book will remember that the Bianca and Nico turn out to be children of Hades.
“Levi, I mean ... he just looks like Nico,” Scobell says of his co-star. “Levi showed up, and he just kind of nailed it right away.”
As for how Percy will fare without Annabeth?
“Annabeth’s gone, yes, and her role in the trio ... she was the knowledgeable one on this whole world, right?” he says.

“You have Thalia and Grover, who have also had a lot of experience on the run,” he adds. “In a way, it’s kind of like that spot is, you know, not filled in, but there is someone there to to help make those decisions.”
More Star-Studded New Cast Members
Decisions, danger, and demigods aren’t the only things in store for our heroes. Another non-negotiable with quests? Run-ins with the gods of Olympus themselves, of course.

Joining the Olympian deities this season is Hera (Ming-Na Wen), Demeter (Jennifer Beals), Aphrodite (Kate McKinnon), Apollo (Hubert Smielecki) and Artemis (Dafne Keen). Season 3 will also be the first time since the show’s premiere that the gods will be seen altogether on Mount Olympus.
As intimidated as Percy is by the gods, so, too, was Scobell by his famous new co-stars.

“I had Jennifer Beals sign a ‘Flash Dance’ poster for me, and I had Ming-Na Wen sign a ‘Mulan’ poster for me,” Scobell says with a laugh. “That was the most nerve-wracking thing I think I’ve ever done on the set of ‘Percy Jackson.’”
What’s Next for Scobell?
As Season 3 debuts, Scobell is experiencing another life milestone: his junior year of high school.
“I don’t know if those two have ever really coincided very well,” he says.
“I don’t think I ever would have been able to do what I do without the help of my school, and then also the help of the set teachers I’ve been blessed with,” he adds.

As for what’s next, Scobell will appear in the upcoming “Angry Birds 3” movie, heading to theaters Dec. 23. He’s also hopeful for a “PJO” renewal for a fourth and fifth season. Scobell says the final two books in the series — “The Battle of the Labyrinth” and “The Last Olympian” — remain his favorites.
“I’ve always said (Book) 5, but you can’t really have the payoff of 5 without 4. So it’s like a ‘Avengers End Game—Infinity War’ situation,” Scobell says.
He also stresses that the show’s adaptation of “The Titan’s Curse” builds up the “intensity” that comes to a head in the final two parts of the story.

“There were points in filming the second and first season that I’m like, ‘I need to get hurt more,’ or like, ‘There needs to be a chance that I die on this quest,’” he says. “And with this, we’re narrowly escaping it every single time.”

title: Kathie Lee and Hoda Bring London Olympics to the Plaza in 2012
summary: Kathie Lee Gifford and Hoda Kotb competed in an obstacle course on the plaza in 2012 to help celebrate the Summer Olympics in London.
story: As TODAY marks its 75th anniversary, the TODAY Archive is revisiting legendary interviews, stories that moved us and other iconic moments from our 75 years on the air. These are the segments that shaped TODAY and created a lasting legacy. Today, we look back at Hoda and Kathie Lee competing in a wacky obstacle course to celebrate the Summer Olympics on July 27, 2012.
Kathie Lee Gifford and Hoda Kotb didn’t just get into the Olympic spirit while hosting the fourth hour of TODAY on July 27, 2012 — the same day that year’s Summer Olympics in London kicked off.
The pair put their athletic ability to the test in an obstacle course, as part of a celebration on the plaza for the Summer Games.

The duo, with a gaggle of interns behind them, walked onto the plaza, each carrying a glass of wine as the Olympic theme played. Hoda was decked out in a red tracksuit, as part of Team Hoda, while Kathie Lee sported blue for Team Kathie Lee. Guests applauded while young girls performed gymnastics.
How Did Hoda and Kathie Lee Hype Up the Obstacle Course?
The obstacle course was part of an all-Olympic-themed show.
“We have the most ridiculous, ridiculous obstacle course known to man,” Hoda said.
“I hear they’ve been taking bets on who’s going to win that one,” Kathie Lee said, prompting Hoda to say the bets were two-to-one for Kathie Lee.
“Where’s the outrage?” Hoda jokingly said.
“I don’t know. I don’t feel it today. It’s game day and I just don’t feel it,” Kathie Lee said.
What Did Hoda and Kathie Lee Have to Do on the Obstacle Course?
“This is going to show our ingenuity, our athletic ability,” Hoda said.
“All that stuff,” Kathie Lee added.
Entertainment Weekly’s Tim Stack was on hand to lay out what they’d have to do.
“This is a complicated course,” Hoda said.

The course featured a cornucopia of events, including spinning around a bat, carrying a glass of wine while walking across a balance beam, tossing a large ring like a hula hoop around an intern and slam dunking a basketball on a lowered basket.
“Hoda has a great advantage like that because she is 8 feet tall!” joked Kathie Lee.
They would also have to open a bottle of wine and race to be the first to put a medal around someone’s head at the end of the course.
How Did the Competition Go?
Kathie Lee took an early lead, but Hoda stormed back when she dunked. They were virtually tied when it came time to open the wine.
Kathie Lee had a cape put on her and was given a medal, which she successfully placed around the person’s neck, giving her the victory and earning her an oversized medal.
Hoda was hardly a sore loser, though.
“You guys, that rocked!” she said.

title: ‘DWTS’ Semifinals Ends With Bittersweet Elimination as These 5 Couples Head to the Finale
summary: Read all about what went down during the Nov. 17 “DWTS” semifinals, including the dances, scores of each couple and who got eliminated.
story: It’s officially the semifinals on “Dancing With the Stars” and the six remaining couples are just a couple dances away from making it to the Season 35 finale.
The Nov. 17 episode kicked off with co-hosts Alfonso Ribeiro and Julianne Hough welcoming viewers to the second to last episode.
Last week saw the shocking and unexpected elimination of Jenna Dewan and partner Valentin Chmerkovskiy — and one more couple will take their last bow tonight.
Carrie Ann Inaba, Bruno Tonioli and Derek Hough are judging the last pairs as they each perform one final ballroom and Latin dance style to prove they are worthy of the Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy.
A Recap of the Individual Dances

Connor Wood and partner Rylee Arnold were the first couple to compete and received mixed reactions. Bruno said that while he was bursting with excitement, he lost the timing towards the end. Carrie Ann told him to enjoy the moment more, while Derek did say he saw his excitement, but called some technical stuff out.
His second dance received more constructive criticism, while Carrie Ann got out of her seat to give him a hug and tell him he shouldn’t be nervous.

Harry Shum Jr. showed off his paso doble skills, delivering a fiery routine with Jenna Johnson that got Carrie Ann on her feet, calling it a “paso doble of the season.” Derek applauded him for his command and authority on the floor. For his second dance, a quickstep, Carrie Ann was blown away, while Derek said there was an intensity to Harry that had it all. Bruno called it “impeccable” in every way.

When it came to Maura Higgins’ samba, Derek called it “beautifully satisfying” and “impressive.” Bruno and Carrie Ann were utterly stunned by how she hit every move and executed it perfectly. For her Viennese waltz, Bruno called her haute couture and a beautiful way of showing her skills. Carrie Ann did note a strain in her neck, but still enjoyed the routine.

Ezra Frech’s quickstep got a round of applause from the audience and judges, who commented on his frame and momentum. Derek called him the definition of defying the odds. For his second dance, a jive, Carrie Ann got up and said it was so entertaining, Derek and Bruno also gave him his flowers for his accomplishments this season.

Amber Glenn’s salsa “lit up the ballroom,” according to Carrie Ann. Derek said she made a “statement” with her “professional-level routine,” while Bruno said it was “sal-sational.” The Olympian’s Viennese waltz had Carrie Ann telling her she “earned a spot in the finale” and Derek called it sultry and sensual and that she was the most consistent competitor. Bruno said she doesn’t miss a beat.

Closing out the first round was Tatyana Ali with a waltz that made her look like a “glittery goddess.” He also complimented her extensions and for listening to their feedback. Carrie Ann said her dancing makes people believe they too can dance beautifully. Her cha cha had Derek telling her she had great energy but did comment on some technical details like the foot placement, as did Bruno. Carrie Ann, however, called it perfection and gave them their first 10.

title: Jennifer Lopez Says She’s the ‘Happiest I’ve Been’ and Credits This 1 Change in Her Love Life
summary: Jennifer Lopez says she’s single, opens up about her divorces and the ‘JLo Show’ in new interview with Hoda Kotb on the TODAY show and podcast ‘Making Space.’
story: After decades in the public eye and four divorces, Jennifer Lopez is no stranger to love, both feeling and talking about it. The complex emotion was a major theme in her lengthy sit-down with friend and former TODAY anchor Hoda Kotb, which aired in part on TODAY Nov. 17. The full extended version will be available as an episode of  the “Making Space” podcast Nov. 18.

“The thing for me is to be the love in the room,” Lopez, 57, told Hoda, 62. “To put love out into the world. To remind people that love exists. ... Love yourself and remember who you are. I’ve been on that journey, and once you remember who you are, you wanna remind others. ... I feel like for me, since (I was) very young, without knowing it, that’s been my purpose.”

Hoda then revealed that one of the qualities she admires most about Lopez is her ability to fall in love. That prompted Hoda to share that she’s not sure if she’s ever been in love herself — “which gives me chills, and also makes me a little sad because it takes guts,” Hoda added.
“It takes a fearlessness,” Lopez responded before explaining why she’s fine without having romantic love at the moment.

“What you realize is what you’re searching for in another person is only up to you,” Lopez explained. “I have the ability to fall in love every day with my life, with the cup of coffee, with the bath, with the song I created that day.”
“The only way you really learn these lessons is to make mistakes, to fail, to have things not work out the way you thought they were.”
“It’s been kind of a two or three-year journey for me of really trying to understand myself, what my purpose is and what love is. And that for me has been a joy.”
She said she’s since realized that love isn’t what makes you happy, but rather that you should make yourself happy.

“You have to really understand that that is in your hands, and it’s how you wake up every day. ... It’s how you choose to walk through the world, understanding your power, understanding everything about yourself that is only you uniquely and what you have to offer to the world. And I think for me, that made me look at romantic relationships differently, as well, because it’s not something that I need. It’s something that I would like.”
“I have been the happiest I’ve been the past few years, where I’ve been single,” Lopez laughed. “But it took time to get there for me because I was such and I still am very much romantic.”
Lopez is now able to see the positive in this mindset though, she told Hoda.

“I used to beat that part of myself up. Like, that’s the reason I made these choices and these mistakes, and I’ve had these failures. ... I’ve been divorced several times. My kids didn’t have the things that I wanted them to have.”
“And then you realize ... that romantic is the person who is able to go out into the world and create a life that I could have never dreamed of when I was growing up in the Bronx.”

She said she sometimes struggled with how much of her personal life she made public. “I felt like it really overshadowed some of the work that I did and the things that I was really proud of ... And hurt me with opportunities as well, I think.”

“Your star celebrity part of you becomes bigger than the work that you’re doing. And I would look at other people’s careers and go, ‘Why don’t they get this type of scrutiny? Why is it me?’” she chuckled.

“I have to take responsibility in that I was very open about my life. I’ve never been kind of a guarded person in that way. I always wore my heart on my sleeve and was a very open book. And what I realize is that you have to have boundaries. That’s part of loving yourself. That’s part of it.”

A recent, major change in Lopez’s life that’s allowed her more time to reflect is becoming an empty nester. Her twins, whom she shares with ex-husband Marc Anthony, recently left for college. But, like any other parent, she helped them decorate their rooms, sobbed and went on her way.

“It was the first time I’ve lived alone in I don’t know how long, so that was really weird,” Lopez recalled. “Not having them down the hall does something to your heart. But I also realized I do enjoy my own company.”

“I enjoy my space, and I never was like that. I was always so afraid of the quiet and of being alone. I think that’s what drove me to make some decisions that weren’t the best for me in my life. But I really feel at peace there in my house that I’ve built.”
This major lifestyle change has helped inspire her in the recording studio, as well.

“I’ve made some songs that really feel very me right now. They’re a little bit unapologetic. They’re very different than things that I’ve dared to write before,” Lopez said. “A lot of 20-year-olds ... make the pop music. I made the pop music when I was in my 20s, and I write for me and for people who experience what I’m experiencing. And it’s a different type of feeling. I think it’s important to do that, to have that voice out there, too.”

The rom-com star is also focused on another creative project: the Thanksgiving Day release of her concert film, “The JLo Show: Live From Las Vegas.” The title is a play on how public her life has been over the past few decades.

“Yes, you’re watching ‘The JLo Show,’ me singing and dancing. But also, I started out watching ‘West Side Story’ on Thanksgiving in front of that TV, thinking about being an entertainer. I never thought that also my life, my personal life, would become the show and everything about me would be fair game,” Lopez explained.

“I didn’t think about the fame side of this. I just thought, ‘I wanna sing and dance and act. That’s what I wanna do with my life.’ This other part that comes along with it. And so, it’s a real, interwoven piece about a mini-musical of my life.”
So what’s next for the icon in her personal life? She told Hoda she’s setting boundaries and open to romantic partnership if it comes her way — but not just with anyone.

“You get to a point where you have a certain standard, because if I’m on the floor or if I’m up here, it doesn’t matter,” Lopez said. “Is there somebody who can match who you are and the love that you’re capable of giving?”
“Life is gonna take you in all those different directions, but having somebody who sees you and loves you in all of those iterations is really the goal.”

The full “Making Space” episode with Jennifer Lopez comes out November 18th. Watch it on YouTube or listen on Spotify. Check out Season 9 of “Making Space” for conversations with Ina Garten, Mariska Hargitay, Sandra Bullock and more!
